q: 端到端延迟目标定为 < 200ms，这个数字的依据是什么？
options: 建立连接的三次握手大约耗时 200ms 左右
本设计选定的体验目标，不是协议强制值
服务器推流协议规范里规定的最大间隔
内容分发网络边缘缓存的默认刷新周期
why: 200ms 不是硬分界，而是本设计采用的实时体验目标：低于这个量级通常会被感知为很快、接近即时。更严格的交互目标常会用 100ms 量级。
why_en: Two hundred milliseconds is a practical realtime target rather than a hard perception boundary; interactions under that range usually feel very fast, while stricter instant-feedback targets are often closer to 100ms.
options_en: The connection three-way handshake takes about 200ms.
This design's chosen target, not a protocol requirement.
The maximum interval defined by the server-push spec.
The default refresh period for the content delivery network cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序可靠传输的传输层协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

scenario: 面试官问你为什么把端到端延迟目标定在 200ms，而不是直接照抄某个协议或基础设施参数。
q_en: Why is the end-to-end latency target set below 200ms?
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why the end-to-end latency target is 200ms instead of copying a protocol or infrastructure number.
optionExplanations: 建立连接的三次握手通常几十毫秒量级，跟 200ms 这个体验目标没有因果关系，是无关的巧合数字。
对，200ms 是团队自己定的体验目标，不是照抄某个协议或基础设施参数。
SSE 协议本身不规定端到端延迟上限，把协议条文当成体验目标的依据是张冠李戴。
CDN 边缘缓存的刷新周期是另一层的运维参数，跟评论要多快到达观众无关。
optionExplanations_en: The handshake takes tens of milliseconds, but that has no causal link to a chosen UX latency target.
Right — 200ms is the team's own experience target, not copied from a protocol or infra spec.
SSE itself sets no end-to-end latency ceiling, so citing the spec here confuses protocol with product goal.
A CDN's cache refresh interval is an unrelated ops parameter, not the reason for a comment latency target.

scenario: 直播评论系统：不同观众看到同一条评论的时间略有先后完全无伤大雅，但评论区整体不可用会毁掉直播体验。
q: 非功能需求上该怎么做 CAP 取舍？
options: 一致性优先：所有观众必须在同一瞬间看到同一条评论
放弃分区容忍，假设网络永不分区
可用性优先、接受最终一致：评论晚几百毫秒到达没关系
用分布式事务同时保证强一致和高可用
why: 评论属于典型的可容忍短暂不同步的数据，所以可用性优先、最终一致即可。这条取舍直接决定了后面能用 DynamoDB、Redis pub/sub 这类偏可用的组件。
why_en: Live comments tolerate brief staleness, so the system prioritizes availability over consistency and accepts eventual consistency.
whenOtherWins: 涉及钱、库存扣减、订单这类不能读到旧值的业务必须倒向强一致，宁可短暂拒绝服务。
tradeoff: 可用性优先(最终一致) vs 强一致性
options_en: Consistency first: every viewer must see a comment at the exact same instant.
Drop partition tolerance and assume the network never partitions.
Availability first with eventual consistency: comments landing a few hundred ms late is fine.
Use distributed transactions to guarantee strong consistency and high availability together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统里一致性、可用性、分区容忍性三者的取舍框架
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the tradeoff among consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短暂不同步，但保证副本最终收敛到相同值
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows brief staleness but guarantees replicas converge over time.

q_en: How should we make the CAP tradeoff for live comments?
scenario_en: In live comments, viewers can see the same comment slightly apart in time, but an unavailable comment experience ruins the live stream.
optionExplanations: 转账、扣库存这类不能读到旧值的场景才该一致性优先；评论慢半秒没人在意，为此牺牲可用性不值。
现实网络会分区，是分布式系统必须面对的常态，假设它不存在直接违背 CAP 的前提。
对，几百毫秒的到达差异对观众无伤；把服务保持在线，比让所有人同一刻看到同一条更重要。
CAP 下强一致和高可用不可兼得，分布式事务只是把代价转嫁成延迟或阻塞，不是真的兼得。
optionExplanations_en: Consistency-first fits money or inventory flows that can't read stale values; comments arriving late is harmless, so paying for it here is wasteful.
Real networks do partition, so assuming they never will breaks the basic premise CAP is built on.
Right — a few hundred milliseconds of skew is harmless here; keeping the experience online matters more than synchronized delivery.
CAP says you can't have both strong consistency and high availability; distributed transactions just hide the cost as extra latency or blocking.

q: FB Live Comments 的规模（scale）目标是？
options: 数百万路并发直播，热门场每秒数千条评论
全平台只有几千路直播，每场每秒也就几条评论
只有一路超级直播，累计百万条评论总量
只需支撑工作日高峰的几万观众，无并发压力
why: 规模需求是双重的：横向是数百万路并发视频，纵向是热门单场每秒数千条评论。后面的分层方案（pub/sub、采样、CDN）就是围绕这两个维度展开的。
why_en: The system must scale to millions of concurrent live videos with thousands of comments per second on a single hot video.
options_en: Millions of concurrent live videos, thousands of comments per second on a hot one.
Only a few thousand live videos platform-wide, a handful of comments per second each.
A single mega live video with a million comments in total.
Only needs weekday-peak traffic of a few tens of thousands of viewers.
scenario: 面试官让你先说清楚这套评论系统要扛住的规模量级，再继续往下设计。
q_en: What scale should FB Live Comments be designed for?
scenario_en: Before designing further, the interviewer asks you to state the order of magnitude the comment system must handle.
optionExplanations: 对，横向数百万路并发视频、纵向热门单场每秒数千条评论，这两个维度撑起了后面的分层方案。
几千路、每场几条评论这个量级远小于题目要求，撑不起后面对推送层和采样的深挖。
把总量压缩成单路直播的百万评论，漏掉了并发路数这个维度，规模判断会整个偏小。
只按工作日高峰的几万观众来设计，会让后面的横向扩展和采样方案变得没有必要。
optionExplanations_en: Right — millions of concurrent videos plus thousands of comments per second on a hot one drives everything that follows.
A few thousand videos with a handful of comments each is far below the stated scale and skips the reason for push and sampling.
Collapsing it to one video with a million comments total drops the concurrency dimension entirely.
Sizing only for tens of thousands of weekday-peak viewers makes the later horizontal scaling and sampling work unnecessary.

q: 对这类 product 风格的系统设计题，推荐的推进策略是？
options: 先把所有深挖点讲完，最后再补高层架构图
先做完整容量估算，数字齐了再动手设计
从完整的数据库 schema 开始，自底向上推
按功能需求逐条推进，再用非功能需求叠深度
why: 策略是顺序推进：一条条满足功能需求，保证不迷失在细节里；功能齐了以后，再让非功能需求引导深挖和复杂度。
why_en: Build the design sequentially through each functional requirement, then use the non-functional requirements to layer on depth.
options_en: Cover every deep dive first and only then draw the high-level diagram.
Do a full capacity estimate and start designing once the numbers are in.
Start from a complete database schema and build bottom-up.
Work through the functional requirements in order, then layer depth from the non-functional ones.
q_en: How should you approach this product-style system design interview?
optionExplanations: 先讲深挖点会让面试官看不到全局，一头扎进细节容易迷路，拖慢整体节奏。
容量估算通常按需插入设计过程中，不必在动手前做一次完整估算。
过早定死 schema 会在后续需求逐步展开时被迫返工，字段还没到该确定的阶段。
对，先逐条满足功能需求打好地基，再让非功能需求引导深挖，是稳妥的推进节奏。
optionExplanations_en: Leading with deep dives buries the interviewer in detail before they see the big picture and stalls momentum.
Capacity estimates are usually folded in as the design needs them, not done wholesale before anything else.
Locking the schema too early forces rework once later requirements reshape which fields you actually need.
Right — work through each functional requirement first to build a foundation, then let non-functional needs drive the depth.
scenario: 45 分钟面试设计 FB Live 评论区，功能需求已列全，非功能需求还没深挖，时间必须省着花。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes for Facebook Live comments: the functional requirements are listed, the non-functional ones aren't explored yet, and time is tight.

q: 补全三个核心实体：
text: 本题只有三个核心实体：{{User}}（既可以是观众也可以是主播）、{{Live Video}}（由其他团队管理、需要集成的直播视频）、{{Comment}}（用户发在直播上的消息）。
why: 实体是系统的「名词」：User、Live Video、Comment。其中 Live Video 归别的团队所有，我们只做集成。
why_en: The three core entities are the user, the live video owned by another team, and the comment posted on it.
q_en: Fill in the three core entities.

q: 为什么开局只列核心实体、而不直接给完整数据模型？
options: 早期定不准字段，先立核心名词打地基，schema 随设计补全
数据模型在面试里不重要，可以全程跳过不谈
面试官通常不会看你的 schema 设计，写了也白写
实体列表和完整 schema 本质是同一件事，写哪个都行
why: 开局阶段还无法准确枚举所有列/字段，硬写只会返工。先立住核心实体来引导思路，数据模型随设计逐步长出来。
why_en: Early in the design you cannot enumerate every column yet, so you start with core entities and grow the data model as the design progresses.
options_en: You can't pin down fields this early, so name the core entities first and let the schema fill in as the design grows.
The data model doesn't matter in interviews, so you can skip it entirely.
Interviewers never look at your schema, so writing one is wasted effort.
An entity list and a full schema are the same thing, so either one will do.
q_en: Why start with core entities instead of a full data model?
optionExplanations: 对，设计早期还定不准每个字段，先立住核心名词打地基，字段随设计逐步长出来。
数据模型仍然要在设计推进中补全，跳过它会让后续讨论缺了地基。
面试官通常会追问字段细节，说他们不关心 schema 不成立。
实体列表只是「名词」清单，完整 schema 需要更多信息才能定，两者不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Right — you can't pin down every field yet, so naming the core entities first gives the design a foundation to grow from.
The data model still gets filled in as the design progresses; skipping it entirely leaves no foundation.
Interviewers routinely probe field-level detail, so claiming they don't care about the schema doesn't hold.
An entity list is just the noun list; a full schema needs information you don't have yet, so the two aren't the same thing.
scenario: FB Live 评论区设计的第 5 分钟：后面还要加分页、推送、CDN，字段肯定还会反复变。
scenario_en: Five minutes into the Facebook Live comments design — pagination, push and CDN are still coming, so the fields will keep changing.

scenario: 设计发评论的 POST 接口，必须防止用户篡改请求、冒充他人发评论。
q: userId 应该从哪里来？
options: 放进请求体，由客户端自行填写 userId 字段
作为 URL 查询参数随请求传入
服务端从头部令牌中解析出身份
从 cookie 里直接读取明文 userId
why: 客户端只负责携带令牌，服务端校验令牌并从中提取 userId。身份不走请求体，用户就无法伪造 userId 冒充别人，这是现代 Web 应用的通用做法。
why_en: The server extracts the user id from a validated JWT or session token in the header, which prevents users from tampering with the request to impersonate others.
whenOtherWins: 内部受信服务间调用或管理后台代用户操作时，可以在请求体里显式传目标 userId，但仍要有服务级鉴权。
options_en: Put userId in the request body for the client to fill in.
Pass userId as a URL query parameter.
Server parses identity from the header token.
Read plaintext userId straight from a cookie.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON Web Token，一种把用户身份编码进已签名令牌的方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes a user's identity claims.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端签发、代表已登录会话的令牌
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session token represents an authenticated session issued by the server.

tradeoff: 令牌解出身份 vs 请求体自报身份
q_en: Where should the userId come from?
scenario_en: You are designing the POST API for comments and must prevent users from tampering with the request to impersonate someone else.
optionExplanations: 内部受信服务之间可以显式在请求体传目标 userId，但面向普通用户时任何人都能改这个字段冒充别人。
URL 查询参数和请求体一样是客户端能直接编辑的内容，同样挡不住伪造身份。
对，签名令牌把身份绑定在服务端可校验的数据里，客户端没有密钥就不能改成别人。
明文 cookie 没有签名校验，用户或中间人一样能直接改写里面的 userId。
optionExplanations_en: Trusted internal services can pass a target userId explicitly in the body, but a public client can edit that same field to impersonate anyone.
A URL query parameter is just as editable by the client as the body, so it offers no real protection either.
Right — the signed token binds identity to data the server can verify, and the client can't rewrite it as another user.
A plaintext cookie carries no signature check, so a user or a man-in-the-middle can rewrite the userId just as easily.

q: 读这个创建评论的请求，正确的说法是？
options: userId 应补进请求体，方便服务器直接识别用户
liveVideoId 应该放进请求体而不是路径
这个 POST 请求会顺带返回该视频最近一页的历史评论
视频 ID 走路径参数，评论内容走请求体，身份从令牌头解析
why: 写接口极简：路径定位视频，body 只带 message，身份由头部令牌承载。查历史评论是另一个 GET 接口的职责。
why_en: The create-comment endpoint takes the video id in the path, the message in the body, and the user identity from the auth token header.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as API
    participant M as Comment Service
    participant D as Comment DB
    participant P as Push path
    C->>A: POST /comments
    A->>M: auth user + liveVideoId
    M->>D: append comment
    M->>P: publish new comment
options_en: userId should be added to the body so the server can identify the user directly.
liveVideoId should live in the request body instead of the path.
This POST also returns the video's latest page of comment history.
The video id goes in the path, the message in the body, and identity comes from the auth token header.
q_en: What is the correct read of this create-comment request?
optionExplanations: 身份应该来自已签名令牌，让客户端自报 userId 会重新打开伪造身份的口子。
liveVideoId 本就是要定位的资源，属于路径参数，不需要塞进请求体。
历史列表属于读取历史的接口；这条 POST 只表达「新增一条评论」这个动作。
对，视频 ID 走路径定位资源、评论内容走 body、身份从令牌头解析，三者各司其职。
optionExplanations_en: Identity should come from a signed token, not from letting the client self-report userId — that reopens the impersonation hole.
liveVideoId identifies the resource being addressed, so it belongs in the path, not stuffed into the body.
History belongs to the read-history endpoint; this POST only represents appending one new comment.
Right — the video id locates the resource in the path, the message goes in the body, and identity comes from the token header.
scenario: FB Live 写评论接口：观众在直播页发一条评论，身份已由网关校验过的 JWT 令牌承载。
scenario_en: The Facebook Live create-comment endpoint: a viewer posts on the live page and identity already rides in a gateway-validated JWT.

scenario: 用户刚加入直播，页面要先显示加入之前最近的一页评论；之后如果继续往上滚，才加载更早的历史评论。
q: 加载「加入直播之前的历史评论」时，为什么不用已有的 since 参数？
options: since 参数本身查询效率太慢
since 参数不支持设置每页返回多少条评论
since 只能配合写路径一起使用
since 给的是比锚点更新的评论，方向反了
why: 对，历史评论应该用 cursor/before + limit。since 是「给我锚点之后的新评论」，适合断线后追赶；历史回看要「锚点之前的 N 条」，方向相反。
why_en: Yes: historical comments should use cursor/before plus limit. since means comments newer than the anchor, which is useful for catching up after disconnects; history loading needs the N comments before an anchor.
codeSample:
GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?limit=20
# 返回最近 20 条历史评论 + nextCursor

GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?before={nextCursor}&limit=20
# 往上滚时，继续取更早的 20 条

GET /live-videos/{liveVideoId}/comments?since={lastSeenCommentId}
# 断线重连时，追赶更新的评论
options_en: The since parameter itself is too slow to query.
The since parameter doesn't support setting how many comments per page.
since only works alongside the write path.
since returns comments newer than the anchor, which is the wrong direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 增量读取参数：返回某个锚点之后的新评论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: since is an incremental-read parameter that returns comments newer than an anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 历史分页参数：用上一页最早那条评论做锚点，继续取它之前的评论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: cursor/before is a history pagination marker that fetches comments older than the oldest item on the current page.

tradeoff: cursor 向历史方向翻页 vs since 向最新方向追赶
q_en: Why not use the existing since parameter to load comments from before joining?
scenario_en: A user has just joined a live video and needs the most recent page of comments from before joining; scrolling up should load older history.
optionExplanations: since 的问题不是查询慢，是方向从一开始就选错了。
分页大小和 since 的语义无关，这不是它不适用的原因。
since 本来就是读路径的参数，跟写路径没有关系。
对，新评论追赶看锚点之后，加入前历史看锚点之前；翻旧页应该走 before/cursor。
optionExplanations_en: since isn't slow to query — the real problem is that it points the wrong direction entirely.
Page size has nothing to do with since's semantics, so that isn't why it's the wrong fit.
since is a read-path parameter to begin with, so pairing it with writes was never the constraint.
Right — catch-up looks after the anchor, while pre-join history looks before it, so old pages use before/cursor.

scenario: 评论是结构简单的记录，没有复杂关系和事务需求，但要求快、可水平扩展、高可用。
q: 评论库选什么？
options: DynamoDB：简单记录的高吞吐存取，可扩展、高可用
图数据库 Neo4j：评论天然是父子图关系
只存 Redis 内存：追求极致的读写速度
必须用 Postgres：评论要跨行事务和外键完整性
why: 评论没有复杂关系或事务需求，DynamoDB 的速度、扩展性和高可用正合适。这不是唯一解，重点是理由要贴需求。
why_en: DynamoDB fits because comments are simple records without complex relationships or transactions, and it is fast, scalable, and highly available.
whenOtherWins: 文章明说 Postgres / MySQL 也完全可行；如果后续要复杂关系查询或事务，关系库反而更顺手。
options_en: DynamoDB: high-throughput access to simple records, scalable and highly available.
Neo4j graph database: comments are naturally parent-child graph relationships.
Keep everything in Redis memory for maximum read and write speed.
Must use Postgres because comments need cross-row transactions and foreign-key integrity.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值数据库，按主键查询扩展性好
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that scales well for key-based queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源关系型数据库，支持事务和复杂查询
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is an open-source relational database that supports transactions and complex queries.

tradeoff: DynamoDB 的速度和扩展性 vs 关系库的事务能力
q_en: Which database should store comments?
scenario_en: Comments are simple records with no complex relationships or transactions, but they need fast reads and writes, horizontal scale, and high availability.
optionExplanations: 对，访问模式是按直播和时间读写简单记录，托管 KV/文档库能少管分片、容量和可用性。
评论之间没有天然的图关系需要遍历，选图数据库是为不存在的查询模式买单。
纯内存存储掉电易失，评论这种要长期保留的数据不能只放 Redis。
评论没有跨行事务需求，把「必须」焊死在 Postgres 上是过度设限。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the access pattern is simple records by video and time, so a managed key-value or document store reduces sharding, capacity, and availability work.
Comments have no inherent graph relationships to traverse, so a graph database pays for a query pattern that isn't there.
Pure in-memory storage loses data on restart, and comments need to persist, so Redis alone isn't enough.
Comments don't need cross-row transactions, so insisting Postgres is mandatory overconstrains the choice.

q: Comment Management Service 的职责是什么？
options: 只负责校验用户是否已登录
负责直播视频流的转码与分发
收发评论：写入评论库并查询返回给观众
负责管理 CDN 的缓存刷新策略
why: 它是评论的读写入口：收到评论后校验并落库，也承担从库里取评论回给观众。视频流本身归别的团队。
why_en: The comment management service creates and stores incoming comments and also queries the database to serve comments back to viewers.
options_en: Only checks whether the user is logged in.
Transcodes and distributes the live video stream.
Handles comments: stores writes and serves reads.
Manages CDN cache refresh policy.
q_en: What is the Comment Management Service responsible for?
optionExplanations: 鉴权只是写路径的一步，把整个服务的职责窄化成校验登录漏掉了读写评论本身。
视频流的转码分发归另一个团队负责，不是评论服务的职责。
对，它是评论的读写入口：写入落库、也负责查询返回给观众。
CDN 缓存刷新策略属于基础设施层，不是评论服务该管的事。
optionExplanations_en: Auth is just one step in the write path; narrowing the whole service down to login checks drops read and write entirely.
Transcoding and distributing the video stream belongs to another team, not the comment service.
Right — it's the read/write entry point for comments: stores writes and also serves reads back to viewers.
CDN cache refresh policy is an infrastructure concern, not something the comment service manages.
scenario: FB Live 评论系统里，视频转码和 CDN 分发归另一个团队，评论侧只有一个后端服务。
scenario_en: In Facebook Live comments, video transcoding and CDN delivery belong to another team; the comment side has one backend service.

q: 「客户端每隔几秒轮询新评论」这个朴素方案的核心缺陷是？
options: 客户端实现轮询与去重逻辑太复杂
近实时要毫秒级轮询，数据库扛不住且多是空跑
轮询无法携带 since 这类增量参数
轮询和无限滚动分页天然互相冲突
why: 观众和评论一多，轮询频率就得跟着涨，数据库压力暴增；而大部分轮询是空手而归的浪费。要满足近实时得毫秒级轮询，不可行。
why_en: Polling cannot scale because near-real-time delivery would require millisecond-level polling that hammers the database while most requests return nothing new.
options_en: Polling plus dedup logic is too complex to implement on the client.
Near-real-time would need millisecond polling, which the database can't sustain and which mostly returns nothing.
Polling cannot carry an incremental parameter like since.
Polling and infinite-scroll pagination are inherently incompatible.
q_en: What is the core flaw in polling for new comments every few seconds?
optionExplanations: 轮询本身实现并不复杂，真正的问题不在客户端代码难度上。
对，要做到近实时就得压到毫秒级轮询，数据库扛不住而且大部分请求都是空手而归。
轮询完全可以带 since 参数，这不是它的短板。
轮询和分页可以配合使用，两者并不天然冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Polling logic itself isn't hard to implement; that's not where the real problem lives.
Right — near-real-time needs millisecond-level polling, which the database can't sustain, and most requests come back empty.
Polling can absolutely carry a since parameter, so that isn't the limitation.
Polling and pagination work fine together; they aren't inherently at odds.
scenario: 一场 100 万观众的直播，新评论要求 200ms 内可见；朴素方案是客户端每几秒轮询一次。
scenario_en: A live video with a million viewers needs new comments visible within 200ms; the naive plan is clients polling every few seconds.

scenario: 面试中你已经很熟这道题，清楚轮询之外更优的推送方案。
q: 起步方案该怎么处理？
options: 假装第一次见这题，从最朴素的轮询开始慢慢推导
直接上更优方案，但要论证决策、讲清权衡
让面试官决定从哪个方案开始讲起
跳过高层设计，直接进入深挖环节
why: 已知更优解就可以直接上，关键是把「为什么」和取舍讲清楚。不必为了表演而绕路。
why_en: If you already know the better solution you can jump straight to it, as long as you justify the decision and explain the trade-offs.
whenOtherWins: 第一次见到的题就该从轮询这类简单方案起步，打好地基，再在深挖阶段逐步升级。
options_en: Pretend it's your first time and slowly derive it from the most naive polling.
Jump straight to the better solution, but justify the decision and spell out the trade-offs.
Let the interviewer decide which approach to start from.
Skip the high-level design and go straight into deep dives.
q_en: How should you present the starting design?
scenario_en: In the interview, you already know this problem well and know that push beats polling for the realtime comment path.
optionExplanations: 真的是第一次遇到这题时，从轮询起步打地基才合理；已经很熟就没必要装作不会。
对，已经知道更优解就可以直接上，关键是把决策理由和取舍讲清楚，不用为了表演绕远路。
面试节奏该由候选人主导，把起点甩给面试官会显得准备不足。
跳过高层设计会让面试官看不到你从需求到方案的推导过程。
optionExplanations_en: If this really were your first time seeing the problem, starting from polling to build up would make sense; pretending otherwise once you already know better wastes time.
Right — if you already know the stronger solution you can go straight to it, as long as you explain the decision and trade-offs instead of performing a detour.
You should drive the interview's pace yourself; handing the starting point to the interviewer looks underprepared.
Skipping the high-level design hides the reasoning path from requirements to solution that the interviewer wants to see.

q: 用户刚加入一场直播时，评论区要同时满足哪两件事？（多选）
options: 立即开始实时收到新发布的评论
能往上滚动、逐步加载更早的历史评论（无限滚动）
自动回放整场直播视频
把全部旧评论一次性推到屏幕上
why: 加入直播的用户需要两条路径：实时流拿新评论 + 分页拉历史评论。历史部分用聊天应用常见的无限滚动交互。
why_en: A joining viewer needs both a real-time stream of new comments and paginated history loaded through infinite scrolling.
options_en: Immediately start receiving new comments in real time.
Scroll up to progressively load older history via infinite scroll.
Automatically replay the entire live video.
Dump every old comment onto the screen at once.
q_en: When a user joins a live video, what two things must the comment UI handle?
optionExplanations: 挡住的是「错过现场」的风险：实时流让刚加入的观众马上跟上正在发生的讨论。
挡住的是「一次性拉全量」的压力：无限滚动按需分页加载历史，减轻服务器和带宽负担。
自动回放整场视频是播放器的职责，不属于评论区要解决的问题。
一次性推送全部旧评论会在加入瞬间打爆带宽和渲染，跟无限滚动的按需加载正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: It blocks the risk of missing the live moment: a real-time stream lets a joining viewer catch up to the conversation immediately.
It relieves the pressure of loading everything at once: infinite scroll paginates history on demand instead.
Auto-replaying the entire video is the player's job, not something the comment UI needs to solve.
Dumping every old comment at join time spikes bandwidth and rendering — the opposite of on-demand infinite scroll.
scenario: 观众中途点进一场已经播了 40 分钟的直播，评论区此刻是空白的。
scenario_en: A viewer joins a live video 40 minutes in, and the comment pane is currently blank.

q: 在高速滚动的评论流里，offset 分页有哪两大问题？
options: 要数过 offset 之前的所有行，增删还会让偏移错位
offset 不支持自定义的排序方向
offset 分页天生无法配合无限滚动这种交互模式
offset 值本身会泄露用户的隐私信息
why: offset 分页既低效（每页都要扫过前面所有行）又不稳定（滚动期间的新增/删除让偏移失准）。快速变化的评论流正好把两个短板都踩中。
why_en: Offset pagination is slow because the database counts all preceding rows, and unstable because inserts or deletes shift the offset and cause duplicated or missing comments.
options_en: The database counts every row before the offset, and inserts or deletes shift that offset out of place.
Offset does not support a custom sort direction.
Offset pagination inherently cannot work with an infinite-scroll interaction.
The offset value itself leaks user privacy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用数字偏移量跳过前面若干行的分页方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset pagination skips a fixed number of preceding rows using a numeric offset.

q_en: What are the two big problems with offset pagination in a fast comment stream?
optionExplanations: 对，每页都要扫过前面所有行效率低，滚动期间的增删又让偏移错位，快速变化的流正好踩中两个短板。
排序方向和分页方式是两回事，跟 offset 本身无关。
offset 技术上仍能配合滚动加载，问题不在交互模式的兼容性。
offset 只是个数字偏移量，本身不携带任何隐私信息。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the database has to count every row before the offset, and inserts or deletes during scroll shift it out of place, hitting both weaknesses in a fast-moving stream.
Sort direction is a separate concern from pagination style, unrelated to offset itself.
Offset pagination can technically still drive infinite scroll, so compatibility isn't the issue.
An offset is just a numeric position; it carries no privacy information on its own.
scenario: 热门直播每秒新增上千条评论，客户端要一页 20 条地往上翻历史。
scenario_en: A hot live video adds a thousand comments per second while the client pages backwards 20 at a time.

scenario: 高吞吐、评论持续插入的无限滚动列表，要求翻页高效且不会因新评论到来而错位。
q: 分页方案选什么？
options: offset 分页，实现简单直接、前端也好写
每次全量拉取评论，交给客户端自己裁剪
cursor 分页：用评论 ID 做翻页锚点
随机抽取一页评论展示给用户，减少扫描
why: 游标锚定到具体一条评论上：配合索引不用扫过前面的行，增删也不影响游标指向，性能随数据量增长保持稳定，还天然契合 DynamoDB 的 key 查询。
why_en: Cursor pagination anchors on a unique comment id, staying efficient with an index and stable under concurrent inserts, which suits a fast-moving feed.
whenOtherWins: 数据集小、基本静态，或产品需要「跳到第 N 页」时，offset 只传数字偏移，更简单够用。
diagram:
graph LR
    Client[Join live] --> API[GET comments before cursor]
    API --> DB[(Comments by liveVideoId)]
    DB --> Page[Recent page]
    Page --> SSE[Start live SSE]
    SSE --> Client
options_en: Offset pagination — simple to implement and easy on the front end.
Fetch every comment each time and let the client trim the list itself.
Cursor pagination anchored on the comment id.
Randomly sample a page of comments to cut down scanning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用某条记录的唯一 ID 作为翻页锚点的分页方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination anchors each page on a unique record id.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用数字偏移量跳过前面若干行；评论仍可有 ID，只是不用 ID 当翻页锚点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset pagination skips a numeric number of rows; comments can still have ids, but ids are not the page anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值数据库，按主键查询扩展性好
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that scales well for key-based queries.

tradeoff: cursor 稳定高效 vs offset 简单但会错位
q_en: Which pagination strategy should we use?
scenario_en: An infinite comment list keeps receiving inserts at high throughput, and pagination must stay efficient without shifting under new writes.
optionExplanations: 数据量小、基本静态或需要跳到第 N 页时，offset 只传两个数字确实更省事，但持续插入的流里它会错位。
把裁剪工作丢给客户端意味着每次都要传全量数据，热门直播下带宽和数据库都扛不住。
对，用评论 ID 当锚点，查询可以从索引位置继续走；持续插入也不会改变这个锚点。
随机抽样丢掉了按时间顺序回看的能力，跟无限滚动翻历史的交互需求正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: When data is small, mostly static, or you need to jump to page N, offset's two plain integers are genuinely simpler, but it shifts under a stream that keeps inserting.
Handing trimming to the client means shipping the full comment set every time, which neither bandwidth nor the database survives for a hot video.
Right — using comment id as the anchor lets the query continue from an indexed position, and new inserts do not move that anchor.
Random sampling throws away chronological order, the opposite of what scrolling back through history needs.

q: 读这个 DynamoDB（NoSQL 键值库）查询，它返回的是什么？
options: lv_42 中比 c_1088 更新的最近 10 条评论
lv_42 中早于 c_1088 的最近 10 条，新→旧
对整表做全量扫描后任取 10 条
恰好等于 c_1088 的那一条评论
why: commentId < :cursor 限定「比游标更早」，ScanIndexForward=false 表示按 key 倒序（新→旧），Limit 取一页。这正是无限滚动往上翻历史的查询。
why_en: The query fetches the ten most recent comments older than the cursor for that video, sorted newest first, which is exactly one page of history.
options_en: The 10 most recent comments in lv_42 that are newer than c_1088.
The 10 most recent comments in lv_42 older than c_1088, newest first.
Ten arbitrary rows from a full table scan.
The single comment whose id equals c_1088.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值数据库，按主键查询扩展性好
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that scales well for key-based queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用某条记录的唯一 ID 作为翻页锚点的分页方式
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination anchors each page on a unique record id.

q_en: What does this DynamoDB query return?
optionExplanations: 这里的范围条件把结果限制在锚点之前，所以把它解释成更新评论是读错方向。
对，范围条件取旧记录，倒序返回最近的一页；这是往上滚动时需要的结果。
查询带着明确的 KeyConditionExpression 过滤条件，不是无差别的全表扫描。
< 是范围条件，会匹配一批记录，不是精确匹配单条评论。
optionExplanations_en: The range predicate selects records before the anchor, so treating the result as newer comments reads the direction backwards.
Right — the range selects older records and returns the nearest page in descending order, exactly what upward scrolling needs.
The query carries an explicit KeyConditionExpression filter, not an unfiltered full-table scan.
< is a range condition matching a batch of records, not an exact match on a single comment.
scenario: 无限滚动往上翻历史评论：客户端手上只有当前屏幕最旧的一条 commentId = c_1088。
scenario_en: Infinite scroll going back in history: all the client holds is the oldest comment id on screen, c_1088.

q: 补全 cursor 分页的优点：
text: cursor 分页更{{高效}}（有索引时不用数过游标之前的行）、更{{稳定}}（滚动期间的增删不会让游标错位）、契合 DynamoDB 的 {{key}} 式查询，且评论量增长时性能保持{{一致}}。
why: 这四点就是选 cursor 而不是 offset 的完整理由：效率、稳定性、与存储引擎的契合、规模下的性能一致性。
why_en: Cursor pagination is efficient, stable under concurrent changes, a natural fit for key-based queries, and keeps consistent performance as volume grows.
q_en: Fill in the benefits of cursor pagination.

q: 从轮询升级到推送模型，本质上改变了什么？
options: 从客户端猜时机反复问，变成服务端主动推送
把评论从数据库挪到了内存里存放
把底层传输协议从 HTTP 换成了 UDP
把普通的读请求改成了批处理任务
why: 拉模型靠客户端猜时机，猜错就是浪费；推模型让服务端掌握主动权，评论一创建就推出去。这也是协作编辑、实时看板、游戏等实时更新场景的通用模式。
why_en: Instead of clients guessing when to ask, a push model lets the server deliver each comment the moment it is created, the core of the real-time updates pattern.
tradeoff: 服务端主动推送 vs 客户端反复轮询
options_en: From clients guessing and repeatedly asking, to the server pushing proactively.
Moving comments from the database into memory.
Swapping the transport protocol from HTTP to UDP.
Turning normal read requests into batch jobs.
q_en: What fundamentally changes when we move from polling to push?
optionExplanations: 对，拉模型靠客户端猜时机反复问，推模型让服务端一创建评论就主动推出去，主动权换了边。
评论仍然持久化在数据库里，推送模型没有改变存储位置。
SSE 依然跑在标准 HTTP 之上，传输协议并没有换成 UDP。
这跟批处理没有关系，变化的是谁发起动作，不是请求怎么被处理。
optionExplanations_en: Right — instead of clients guessing and asking repeatedly, the server now pushes each comment the moment it's created; the initiative moved sides.
Comments are still persisted in the database; push didn't relocate storage.
SSE still runs over plain HTTP, so the transport wasn't swapped to UDP.
This has nothing to do with batch processing; what changed is who initiates, not how requests get processed.
scenario: 100 万观众的直播要求评论 200ms 内送达，而客户端根本猜不到下一条评论何时产生。
scenario_en: A million-viewer live video needs comments delivered within 200ms, and the client cannot guess when the next one appears.

q: 一句话区分 WebSocket 和 SSE（Server-Sent Events）这两种推送技术？
options: WebSocket 只能单向、SSE 才双向，方向刚好说反了
两者都是双向通道，只是握手方式不同
WebSocket 双向长连接，SSE 单向 HTTP 推流
SSE 不是持久连接，每条消息都要重新建连
why: WebSocket 打开一条双向通道并保持；SSE 只做服务器到客户端的单向推送，且跑在标准 HTTP 上、实现更简单，客户端要发消息就走普通请求。
why_en: WebSockets provide a persistent two-way channel, while SSE is a one-way server-to-client stream over standard HTTP with client messages sent as normal requests.
tradeoff: 双向长连接 vs 单向 HTTP 推流
options_en: WebSocket can only go one-way, SSE is the two-way one — the direction is backwards.
Both are two-way channels, only the handshake differs.
WebSocket is two-way persistent; SSE is one-way over HTTP.
SSE is not persistent, every message needs a new connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单条 TCP 连接上提供全双工双向通信的协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket provides full-duplex two-way communication over a single TCP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: How do WebSocket and SSE differ in one sentence?
optionExplanations: 事实正好相反：WebSocket 才是双向，SSE 是单向服务器推流。
SSE 是单向流，不是双向通道，这个说法把两者都判错了。
对，前者适合双向收发；后者是一条 HTTP 响应流，专门承接服务端连续推给浏览器。
SSE 连接本身是持久的，不需要每条消息都重新建连。
optionExplanations_en: The facts are reversed: WebSocket is the two-way one, SSE is the one-way server push.
SSE is a one-way stream, not a two-way channel, so calling both bidirectional misreads them both.
Right — the former fits two-way traffic; the latter is one HTTP response stream for continuous server-to-browser delivery.
An SSE connection is itself persistent; it doesn't need a fresh connection per message.
scenario: FB Live 评论区：观众绝大多数时间只读评论，偶尔才发一条，要在两种推送技术里选。
scenario_en: In Facebook Live comments viewers mostly just read and only occasionally post, and we have to pick between two push technologies.

scenario: 直播评论的读写极不均衡：绝大多数观众从不发评论，却要持续接收所有评论；发评论本身是低频事件。
q: 推送技术选哪个？
options: WebSocket：为每个观众开一条双向通道
SSE：观众单向收流，发评论走普通 POST
长轮询：兼容性最好，不用引入新协议
gRPC 双向流：性能最强、二进制帧
why: 为几乎只读的观众维护双向通道是白付的开销。SSE 的单向流正好承接高频读，低频写继续用普通 POST，各得其所。
why_en: With reads vastly outnumbering writes, SSE's one-way stream serves viewers efficiently while infrequent comment posts go over plain HTTP.
whenOtherWins: 读写均衡的真双向场景——比如互相频繁收发消息的聊天室——WebSocket 才是最优解。
diagram:
graph LR
    Viewer[Browser viewer] --> SSE[SSE connection]
    Comment[New comment] --> PubSub[Pub/Sub]
    PubSub --> SSE
    SSE --> Viewer
options_en: WebSocket: open a two-way channel for every viewer.
SSE: viewers receive a one-way stream and post comments over plain HTTP POST.
Long polling: best compatibility, no new protocol needed.
Bidirectional gRPC streaming: strongest performance with binary frames.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单条 TCP 连接上提供全双工双向通信的协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket provides full-duplex two-way communication over a single TCP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 HTTP/2 的高性能 RPC 框架，支持双向流
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework built on HTTP/2 that supports bidirectional streaming.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发起请求后服务器 hold 住，直到有数据或超时才响应
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long polling holds a client's request open until new data arrives or it times out.
