optionExplanations: 轮询数据库延迟高，还有大量空查，跟推送要求的实时性正好相反。
两两互连的网格连接数会随服务器数量的平方增长，规模一大就没法维护。
对，评论服务只需发布一次，各推送服务器订阅后各自消费再推给本机观众，写路径和推送方彼此解耦；若还想要集中路由和负载感知规则，Dispatcher 服务是另一个成立的方向。
共享文件当消息总线既不可靠也难扩展，tail 读取本身就有延迟和一致性问题。
optionExplanations_en: Polling the database is high-latency and mostly comes back empty, the opposite of what push needs.
A pairwise mesh's connection count grows with the square of server count, becoming unmanageable at scale.

Right — the comment service publishes once, each push server subscribes and consumes independently, decoupling writers from pushers; if you also want centralized routing or load-aware rules, a dispatcher service is the other valid direction.
A shared file as a message bus is neither reliable nor scalable, and tailing it introduces its own latency and consistency issues.

q: 「所有推送服务器订阅同一个频道」的朴素 pub/sub 在规模上为什么不行？
options: pub/sub 机制本身不保证送达，一定会丢消息
单一频道会把不同视频的评论顺序打乱
订阅方越多，端到端延迟必然超过 200ms
每台服务器都要消费全网评论，本机没观众也一样
why: 单一频道意味着全量广播：一台只服务视频 A 观众的机器，也要消费视频 B、C、D 的所有评论再丢弃。规模一大这份无效功耗就压垮系统。
why_en: With one global channel every server processes every comment across all videos even when none of its viewers care, wasting compute at scale.
options_en: Pub/sub itself guarantees nothing and is bound to drop messages.
A single channel scrambles the ordering of comments from different videos.
More subscribers necessarily push end-to-end latency past 200ms.
Every server has to consume the whole platform comment firehose even when none of its viewers care.
q_en: Why does one global pub/sub channel fail at scale?
optionExplanations: 丢消息不是全局广播模型的症结，跟频道数量的设计没有关系。
pub/sub 不天然打乱消息顺序，单频道的问题不在乱序上。
延迟是否超标取决于具体实现，不是订阅方越多就必然超标。
对，单一频道意味着全量广播，只服务视频 A 观众的机器也要消费并丢弃视频 B、C、D 的评论，规模一大就压垮系统。
optionExplanations_en: Losing messages isn't the flaw in global broadcast — it's unrelated to channel design.
Pub/sub doesn't inherently scramble order, so that isn't what breaks a single channel.
Whether latency crosses 200ms depends on the implementation, not automatically on subscriber count.
Right — one global channel means full broadcast: a server serving only video A's viewers still has to consume and discard every comment from B, C, D, which collapses at scale.
scenario: 全平台同时有上万场直播、每秒几十万条评论，而每台推送服务器只服务其中几十场。
scenario_en: The platform runs tens of thousands of live videos and hundreds of thousands of comments per second, but each push server serves only dozens of them.

q: 为什么用 hash(liveVideoId) % N 分频道，而不是每个直播一个频道？
options: 取模哈希还能保证消息按发布顺序送达每个观众
取模把频道数压到固定上限，避免开无数频道
一个视频一个频道会导致哈希计算冲突
N 个频道能让底层传输延迟天然更低
why: 频道本身有成本，按视频开频道数量失控。哈希取模把任意多的视频装进固定 N 个频道，服务器只订阅自己观众涉及的那几个。
why_en: Hashing video ids into a fixed number of channels bounds the channel count, since one channel per video would be resource-prohibitive for systems like Kafka.
options_en: Modulo hashing also guarantees in-order delivery to every viewer.
Hashing bounds the channel count instead of opening unlimited channels.
One channel per video would cause hash collisions.
N channels inherently lower the underlying transport latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对哈希值取模，把任意多个 key 映射进固定数量的桶
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hashing a key modulo N maps an unbounded number of keys into a fixed number of buckets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

q_en: Why shard channels with hash(liveVideoId) % N instead of one channel per live video?
optionExplanations: 取模哈希不保证消息顺序，这不是它要解决的问题。
对，按视频一对一开频道数量会失控，哈希取模把任意多视频装进固定 N 个桶，服务器只订阅涉及自己观众的那几个。
一个视频一个频道不存在哈希冲突的说法，频道数和碰撞是两回事。
频道数量和底层传输延迟没有直接关系，这是无关的联想。
optionExplanations_en: Modulo hashing doesn't guarantee ordering; that's not the problem it's solving.
Right — one channel per video would let the count spiral, so hashing packs an unbounded number of videos into a fixed N buckets, and each server only subscribes to the few touching its own viewers.
One channel per video wouldn't cause hash collisions — channel count and collisions are unrelated concepts here.
Channel count has no direct bearing on underlying transport latency; that's an unrelated leap.
scenario: 同时进行的直播从几千涨到几十万，而 Redis 频道本身有内存与订阅开销，不能无限开。
scenario_en: Concurrent live videos grow from thousands to hundreds of thousands, and Redis channels cost memory and subscriptions, so we cannot open them without limit.

q: 分好频道之后，round-robin 负载均衡为什么会把效率优化毁掉？
options: 轮询把各视频观众混在一台机上，订阅集合又膨胀
round-robin 分配的流量本身就不均匀
round-robin 会让频道的哈希计算失效
负载均衡器会因此变成写入瓶颈
why: 频道分区的收益取决于「一台服务器只需要少数频道」；而 round-robin 把观众随机撒开，每台机器的观众什么都看，订阅集合又膨胀回去。解法是智能路由。
why_en: Round-robin scatters viewers of many different videos onto each server, forcing it to subscribe to many channels and reintroducing the inefficiency.
options_en: Round-robin mixes viewers of many videos onto each server, so the subscription set balloons again.
Round-robin distributes traffic unevenly in the first place.
Round-robin breaks the channel hash calculation.
The load balancer turns into a write bottleneck.
q_en: Why does round-robin load balancing ruin the channel optimization?
optionExplanations: 对，轮询把观众随机撒到各台机器，每台都混着各种视频的观众，订阅集合又膨胀回全量。
流量分配是否均匀是另一个话题，不是这里效率被毁掉的原因。
round-robin 只影响观众落在哪台机器，跟频道哈希计算没有关系。
round-robin 影响的是读路径的连接分配，不会让负载均衡器变成写入瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Right — round-robin scatters viewers randomly across machines, so each one ends up with a mix of every video's viewers and the subscription set balloons back out.
Whether traffic lands evenly is a separate question from what breaks the channel optimization here.
Round-robin only decides which machine a viewer lands on; it has nothing to do with the channel hash itself.
Round-robin affects read-path connection placement, not the load balancer's write-side throughput.
scenario: 已按 hash(liveVideoId) % 1000 分好频道，观众连接仍由负载均衡 round-robin 分配。
scenario_en: Channels are already sharded by hash(liveVideoId) % 1000, but viewer connections are still handed out round-robin by the load balancer.

scenario: 希望同一直播的观众尽量落到同一台推送服务器上，让每台服务器只订阅极少数频道。
q: 路由层怎么做？
options: L4 负载均衡只按源 IP 做哈希，四层转发看不到内容
客户端连接失败后随机换一台机器重试
L7 负载均衡按 liveVideoId 做一致性哈希
DNS 轮询把域名解析到不同的服务器 IP
why: 只有 L7 才能看见 liveVideoId 这类应用层信息；按它做一致性哈希，同一视频的观众自然聚到同一台机器，订阅集合就收敛了。
why_en: A layer-7 load balancer can consistent-hash on the video id in the request, keeping viewers of the same video together on the same server.
whenOtherWins: 把 liveVideoId→server 的动态映射放进 Zookeeper 这类协调服务更灵活（可自定义迁移），代价是更高的运维复杂度。
options_en: Layer-4 load balancing hashes only on source IP and forwards without seeing content.
The client retries on a random server after a failed connection.
Layer-7 load balancing that consistent-hashes on liveVideoId.
DNS round-robin resolving the domain to different server IPs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能读取应用层信息（如请求路径）来路由流量的负载均衡器
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-7 load balancer routes traffic using application-level data such as the request path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让同一个 key 稳定映射到同一节点、扩缩容影响小的哈希方法
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps the same key to the same node stably, minimizing disruption when nodes change.

q_en: How should the routing layer work?
scenario_en: We want viewers of the same live video to land on the same push server when possible, so each server subscribes to only a few channels.
optionExplanations: L4 只能按 IP/端口等网络信息转发，无法按正在观看的直播来聚合观众。
随机重试完全不保证同一视频的观众会聚到同一台机器上。
对，只有 L7 才能读懂请求内容按 liveVideoId 做一致性哈希，让同一视频的观众自然聚合；想要更灵活的自定义迁移，代价是把映射放进 Zookeeper 这类协调服务、运维更复杂。
DNS 解析粒度太粗，做不到按单个视频这个维度路由。
optionExplanations_en: L4 can route by network fields like IP and port, but it cannot group viewers by the live video they are watching.
Random retries give no guarantee that viewers of the same video converge on one machine.

Right — only layer-7 can read the request content to consistent-hash on liveVideoId, naturally clustering viewers of the same video; wanting custom migration flexibility instead means pushing the mapping into something like Zookeeper at the cost of more ops complexity.
DNS resolution is too coarse-grained to route by an individual video.

q: 观众协同定位（co-location）方案的主要持续性挑战是？
options: 一致性哈希本身的计算开销太大
NGINX 这类代理不支持处理流式响应
观众会因此完全无法切换到别的直播
观众和服务器都在变化，订阅要持续同步
why: 难点不在建立映射而在维护映射：观众来去、机器增减，负载均衡与 pub/sub 订阅两边的状态要持续对齐。
why_en: The ongoing challenge is coordination: subscriptions must track each server's changing viewer mix, and routing maps must stay in sync as servers scale.
options_en: The computational cost of consistent hashing itself is too high.
NGINX-style proxies do not support streaming responses.
Viewers become completely unable to switch to a different video.
Both viewers and servers keep changing, so subscriptions need constant sync.
q_en: What is the main ongoing challenge with viewer co-location?
optionExplanations: 哈希计算本身很轻量，开销不是持续维护阶段的真正瓶颈。
NGINX 这类代理完全支持流式响应，这个说法与事实相反。
切换到别的直播不受这套路由方案的影响，观众依然能自由换台。
对，关系表会随观众迁移和机器伸缩不停变化；路由层与订阅层必须一起更新。
optionExplanations_en: Hashing itself is computationally light, so that overhead isn't the real bottleneck during ongoing operation.
NGINX-style proxies fully support streaming responses; this claim is the opposite of reality.
Switching to a different stream is unaffected by this routing scheme — viewers can still freely change channels.
Right — the mapping keeps changing as viewers move and servers scale, so routing and subscriptions must be updated together.
scenario: 用一致性哈希把同一场直播的观众固定到少数几台机器，但观众随时进出、机器随时扩缩容。
scenario_en: Consistent hashing pins one video viewers onto a few machines, yet viewers come and go and the fleet scales up and down constantly.

scenario: 不想管理 pub/sub 订阅关系，希望把路由逻辑集中在一处，还想以后加「按服务器负载路由」这类高级规则。
q: 哪种模型正中需求？
options: Dispatcher：按映射转发给目标服务器
把每条新评论无差别广播给系统里所有推送服务器
让客户端定期自己主动拉取新评论
用数据库触发器来驱动评论推送逻辑
why: Dispatcher 把 pub/sub 模型整个反转：服务器不再订阅，由中心组件查映射后点对点投递。路由逻辑集中、好推理，加负载感知等规则也不用改推送服务器。
why_en: A dispatcher service inverts pub/sub by keeping a live map of which servers own which videos and forwarding each comment directly, centralizing the routing logic.
whenOtherWins: pub/sub 通常更简单、边角情况更少，是面试里作者优先推荐的方案。
tradeoff: 集中式 Dispatcher 路由 vs 去中心化 pub/sub 订阅
options_en: Dispatcher: keeps one map, forwards straight to the right server.
Broadcast every new comment indiscriminately to all push servers.
Have clients periodically pull new comments themselves.
Use a database trigger to drive the push logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护路由映射、把消息直接转发到目标服务器的中心组件
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dispatcher is a central component that keeps a routing map and forwards messages directly to servers.

q_en: Which model best matches these requirements?
scenario_en: You want to avoid managing pub/sub subscriptions, centralize routing logic, and later add rules such as routing by server load.
optionExplanations: 对，把转发决策收拢到一个专门组件维护一份映射表，扩展负载感知等新路由规则时只改这一处，不必逐台改推送服务器；不过 pub/sub 通常更简单、边角情况更少，更常被优先推荐。
全量广播给所有服务器正是想避免的浪费，跟集中路由的目标相反。
客户端定期拉取会退化回轮询，满足不了实时推送的需求。
数据库触发器难以承载持续变化的路由逻辑，不是可扩展的推送机制。
optionExplanations_en: Right — routing decisions move into one dedicated component holding a single map, so adding rules like load-aware routing later only touches that one place instead of every push server; pub/sub is usually simpler with fewer edge cases though, so it's the more commonly favored default.
Broadcasting to every server is exactly the waste you're trying to avoid, the opposite of centralized routing.
Having clients pull periodically degrades back into polling, which can't meet the real-time requirement.
A database trigger can't carry constantly-changing routing logic; it isn't a scalable push mechanism.

q: Dispatcher 自己如何避免成为单点？
options: 只能部署单实例，靠快速重启来兜底
多实例共享同一份协调存储中的映射
每个实例各自维护独立映射、互不通信
把映射直接硬编码写进配置文件里
why: Dispatcher 无状态化：映射的权威副本放在 Zookeeper/etcd 里，多实例共享同一份真相，挂一个不影响整体。
why_en: Multiple dispatcher instances run behind a load balancer and all consult the same coordination store like Zookeeper or etcd for consistency.
options_en: Deploy only a single instance and rely on fast restarts.
Multiple instances share one map from a coordination store.
Each instance keeps its own independent map with no sync.
Hard-code the mapping directly into a config file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式协调服务，用来保存和同步共享状态或映射
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zookeeper or etcd is a distributed coordination service for storing and syncing shared state.

q_en: How does the Dispatcher avoid becoming a single point of failure?
optionExplanations: 单实例本身就是单点故障，快速重启解决不了这个结构性问题。
对，把权威映射外置到协调存储，路由节点只做计算和缓存；任一实例挂掉可由其他实例接手。
各实例互不通信会导致映射不一致，路由结果因实例而异。
映射随观众和服务器持续变化，硬编码进静态配置文件跟不上变化。
optionExplanations_en: A single instance is itself the single point of failure; fast restarts don't fix that structural problem.
Right — store the authoritative mapping in coordination storage, let dispatchers compute and cache, and any instance can fail over.
Instances that never sync end up with inconsistent maps, so routing results differ by which instance you hit.
The mapping keeps changing as viewers and servers change, so hard-coding it into static config can't keep up.
scenario: Dispatcher 持有「哪台推送服务器负责哪场直播」的映射，所有评论都要经它转发。
scenario_en: The dispatcher holds the map of which push server owns which live video, and every comment is routed through it.

q: Dispatcher 模型最大的运行期难点是？
options: 转发路径的延迟必然比 pub/sub 更高
Dispatcher 模型无法水平扩展
观众洪流下映射秒级变动，需高频刷新加协同失效
Dispatcher 与 SSE 长连接不兼容
why: 映射的新鲜度就是 Dispatcher 的命门：viral 场景下服务器负责关系秒级变动，任何一份陈旧缓存都会把评论投错地方。
why_en: The dispatcher's hard part is keeping its routing map accurate during rapid change, requiring frequent refreshes and coordinated cache invalidation across instances.
options_en: The forwarding path necessarily has higher latency than pub/sub.
The dispatcher model cannot scale horizontally.
Under viewer churn the map shifts by the second, needing frequent refresh plus coordinated invalidation.
The dispatcher is incompatible with SSE long connections.
q_en: What is the hardest runtime problem in the Dispatcher model?
optionExplanations: 转发延迟高低取决于具体实现，不是 Dispatcher 模型必然的代价。
多实例部署本身就是为了水平扩展，这个说法与实际设计相反。
对，观众换台会让归属关系按秒变化，Dispatcher 得靠心跳或 TTL 主动踢掉过期路由，而不是等转发失败才发现服务器已经不对。
Dispatcher 只负责路由决策，跟 SSE 这类连接协议本身互不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Whether forwarding latency is higher depends on the implementation, not an inherent cost of the dispatcher model.
Running multiple instances is precisely how it scales horizontally, the opposite of this claim.

Right — as viewers hop between videos, ownership shifts by the second, so the dispatcher needs heartbeats or a TTL to actively evict stale entries instead of discovering a bad route only after a forward fails.
The dispatcher only handles routing decisions and has no conflict with a connection protocol like SSE.
scenario: 一场直播突然爆红，观众从 1 万涨到 100 万，推送服务器不停扩容、负责关系秒级变动。
scenario_en: A video goes viral from ten thousand to a million viewers, push servers keep scaling, and ownership changes by the second.

q: 在这个场景下，为什么 Redis pub/sub（发布订阅广播）比 Kafka 更顺手？
options: Kafka 的延迟天生比 Redis pub/sub 更低
Redis 能持久化消息而 Kafka 反而不能
Kafka 能支持的订阅方数量比 Redis 更少
Kafka 应付动态订阅吃力，Redis 更灵活
why: 这里的订阅关系随观众换台不断变动，正是 Kafka 的短板、Redis pub/sub 的长处。维度是「动态订阅的灵活性」，不是吞吐。
why_en: Kafka is scalable and fault-tolerant but struggles with dynamic subscription churn, while Redis pub/sub offers low latency and handles viewers switching videos gracefully.
options_en: Kafka inherently has lower latency than Redis pub/sub.
Redis persists messages while Kafka cannot.
Kafka supports fewer subscribers than Redis.
Kafka struggles with dynamic subscriptions; Redis handles them better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

tradeoff: 动态订阅的灵活性 vs 吞吐与持久化保证
scenario: 推送服务器需要感知观众正在观看哪些直播，而观众会频繁在不同直播间切换，订阅关系持续变动。
q_en: Why is Redis pub/sub a better fit than Kafka in this scenario?
scenario_en: Push servers need to track which live videos their viewers are watching, and viewers switch between live rooms frequently.
optionExplanations: 延迟对比与事实相反：Redis pub/sub 通常比 Kafka 更低延迟，不是 Kafka 更快。
持久化能力的说法正好反了：Kafka 才是能持久化事件日志的一方，Redis pub/sub 是即发即弃。
订阅方数量不是这里的决定因素，两者都能支撑大量订阅者。
对，观众换台会频繁增删订阅；轻量频道订阅更合适，若要持久日志和重放再换 Kafka。
optionExplanations_en: The latency comparison is backwards: Redis pub/sub is typically lower latency than Kafka, not the other way around.
The durability claim is reversed too — Kafka is the one built for a durable event log, while Redis pub/sub is fire-and-forget.
Subscriber count isn't the deciding factor here; both can support large numbers of subscribers.
Right — channel membership changes constantly as viewers switch streams; lightweight subscriptions fit, while durable replay points back to Kafka.

q: Redis pub/sub 是 fire-and-forget（不保证送达），为什么在这里不致命？
options: 评论已持久化在库里，漏掉的靠重连追赶从库或缓存补回
Redis pub/sub 其实内置了消息重试，不会丢
因为还有 Kafka 在后面做兜底队列
观众永远不会感知到任何消息丢失
why: pub/sub 在这里只是「热路径通知」，不是唯一事实来源。数据库兜底 + 追赶机制，让偶发丢消息只是短暂延迟而非数据丢失。
why_en: Fire-and-forget is acceptable because comments are already persisted in the database and the catch-up mechanism recovers anything missed during a brief disconnect.
options_en: Comments are already persisted, so anything missed is refetched from storage or cache by the reconnect catch-up.
Redis pub/sub actually retries internally and never loses messages.
Because Kafka sits behind it as a backup queue.
Viewers will never notice any message loss at all.
q_en: Why is Redis pub/sub being fire-and-forget not fatal here?
optionExplanations: 对，数据库才是唯一事实来源，掉线漏掉的评论靠断线追赶机制从库或缓存补回，pub/sub 只是热路径通知。
Redis pub/sub 本身就是 fire-and-forget，没有内置消息重试。
本设计没有引入 Kafka 做兜底，这里只用了 Redis pub/sub。
短暂断线仍可能让观众错过一两条评论，说完全不会感知太乐观。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the database is the true source of record, so anything missed on a disconnect gets recovered by the catch-up mechanism from storage or cache; pub/sub is only the hot-path notification.
Redis pub/sub is fire-and-forget by design; it has no built-in message retry.
This design never introduced Kafka as a backup — only Redis pub/sub is used here.
A brief disconnect can still cost a viewer a comment or two, so claiming zero perceived loss is overly optimistic.
scenario: 评论先持久化进 DynamoDB 再经 Redis pub/sub 通知推送机；客户端重连时会走追赶补课。
scenario_en: Comments are persisted to DynamoDB first and only then announced over Redis pub/sub, and clients run a catch-up fetch on reconnect.

scenario: 评论服务要把新评论广播出去，推送服务器只想收到与本机观众相关的那部分分片频道的消息。
q: 这组 Redis 命令实现的是什么？
codeSample:
# 推送服务器：按本机观众需要订阅分片频道
SUBSCRIBE comments:shard:7

# 评论服务：hash("lv_42") % 100 = 7，发布到对应分片
PUBLISH comments:shard:7 '{"liveVideoId":"lv_42","commentId":"c_9","message":"nice!"}'
options: 把评论持久化写入数据库存储
分片频道上的发布/订阅广播机制
带延迟投递功能的持久化消息队列
基于 SETNX 命令实现的分布式锁
why: SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH 是 Redis 的 pub/sub 原语；按 hash 分片的频道名让每台服务器只消费自己需要的流量，而不是全网广播。
why_en: These Redis commands implement sharded pub/sub, where only servers subscribed to that hash shard receive the published comment.
whenOtherWins: 需要可回放的持久日志、消费组和严格的吞吐保证时，应该用 Kafka topic 而不是 Redis 频道。
options_en: Persisting the comment write to the database.
A publish/subscribe broadcast on a sharded channel.
A durable message queue with delayed delivery.
A distributed lock built on the SETNX command.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子命令：key 不存在时才写入，常用于实现锁
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SETNX is a Redis command that sets a key only if it is absent, often used to build locks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高吞吐、可持久化的分布式消息日志系统
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a high-throughput distributed log system for durable messaging.

q_en: What do these Redis commands implement?
scenario_en: The comment service needs to broadcast new comments, while push servers only want messages from the shard channels relevant to their local viewers.
optionExplanations: 这组命令不落磁盘；评论持久化应该在数据库写路径完成。
对，按 hash 分片的频道名让服务器只订阅自己需要的那部分流量，是分片广播；要可回放的持久日志和消费组保证时才该换 Kafka。
Redis pub/sub 没有内置的延迟投递能力，这两个命令做不到定时发送。
加锁关注互斥和租约，这里是在频道上广播消息，语义完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: These commands do not write to disk; durable comment storage belongs on the database write path.

Right — the hash-sharded channel name means each server only subscribes to the slice of traffic it needs, i.e. sharded broadcast; switch to Kafka once you need a durable, replayable log with consumer groups.
Redis pub/sub has no built-in delayed delivery; these two commands can't schedule a future send.
Locking is about mutual exclusion and leases; this is channel broadcast, a completely different operation.

scenario: 面试里要在「pub/sub + 观众协同定位」与「Dispatcher 服务」之间选一个作为主推的协调方案。
q: 作者建议优先押哪个？
options: 选 Dispatcher，因为听起来更高级一些
两个方案都完整展开讲，不做取舍
都不选，直接跳到讲 CDN 方案
pub/sub 更简单、边角情况更少，优先押它
why: 两个方案都成立，但 pub/sub 的实现路径更平、坑更少，面试时更容易讲稳。Dispatcher 留作对比加分项。
why_en: Both approaches solve coordination, but pub/sub is typically simpler with fewer corner cases, making it the one to reach for in an interview.
whenOtherWins: 需要集中式路由逻辑、负载感知路由等高级规则时，Dispatcher 的可控性更强。
options_en: Pick dispatcher because it sounds more advanced.
Fully present both without choosing between them.
Skip both and jump straight to the CDN approach.
Pub/sub is simpler with fewer edge cases, so lead with it.
q_en: Which coordination approach should you lead with?
scenario_en: In the interview, you need to choose between pub/sub plus viewer co-location and a Dispatcher service as the primary coordination plan.
optionExplanations: 选型理由应该是工程权衡，不是「听起来高级」这种印象分。
面试时间有限，两个方案都完整展开会显得没有聚焦和判断力。
CDN 方案是另一个独立话题，跳过协调问题本身解决不了跨服务器送达。
对，pub/sub 实现路径更平、边角情况更少，更容易讲稳；需要集中式路由逻辑或负载感知规则时，Dispatcher 的可控性更强，可以留作对比加分项。
optionExplanations_en: The reason to choose should be engineering trade-offs, not that one option merely sounds more advanced.
Interview time is limited; fully presenting both without ever choosing reads as unfocused and indecisive.
The CDN approach is a separate topic; skipping past coordination doesn't actually solve cross-server delivery.

Right — pub/sub has a flatter path with fewer corner cases and is easier to defend under time pressure; when you need centralized routing or load-aware rules, the dispatcher's extra control is worth raising as a bonus comparison.

q: 超级直播每秒 5,000 条评论（平均 4 词一条）意味着什么？
options: 相当于不到 30 秒读完一整本《战争与和平》
数据库会因此先于推送层崩溃宕机
延迟会因此自动涨到 1 秒以上
每条评论平均能在屏幕上停留约 1 秒，足够看清读完
why: 这组数字证明了一个质变：评论流快到超出人类阅读能力时，「每条必达、低延迟」的传统目标失去了意义。
why_en: At five thousand comments per second each message survives about four milliseconds on screen, far beyond human reading speed.
options_en: Equivalent to reading all of War and Peace in under 30 seconds.
The database would crash before the push layer does.
Latency automatically rises above 1 second as a result.
Each comment stays on screen about 1 second on average, long enough to read.
scenario: 世界杯决赛级别的超级直播，评论以每秒 5,000 条的速度涌入，面试官问这组数字说明了什么。
q_en: What does 5,000 comments per second, averaging four words each, imply?
scenario_en: For a World Cup final level live stream, comments arrive at 5,000 per second, and the interviewer asks what that number tells you.
optionExplanations: 对，5,000 条/秒 × 4 词约等于每秒 20,000 词；人眼已无法逐条消费，目标要改成现场感。
先崩溃的说法缺乏依据，这道题的重点是需求本身的质变，不是哪层先扛不住。
延迟涨到多少取决于具体实现，不是数字本身自动导致的结果。
每条评论实际停留的时间远不到 1 秒，这个估算明显偏乐观。
optionExplanations_en: Right — 5,000 comments per second times four words is about 20,000 words per second; people cannot read that, so the target becomes ambience.
Claiming the database crashes first has no basis; the point here is that requirements themselves change, not which layer fails.
How much latency rises depends on the implementation, not something the raw number forces automatically.
Each comment actually survives on screen far less than a second — this estimate is overly optimistic.

q: 评论快到没人能逐条阅读时，系统的设计目标发生了什么变化？
options: 延迟要求反而变得比之前更严格了
必须给每条评论增加送达确认机制
低延迟逐条送达退位，用户要的是氛围
需要把公开评论功能改成私信功能
why: 这是本题最重要的洞察：极端规模下需求本身变了。用户要的是感受到人群的能量，这为采样和 CDN 快照两个方案打开了大门。
why_en: At mega-scale the requirements themselves change: users experience a collective vibe rather than reading individual comments, so strict per-message delivery stops mattering.
options_en: Latency requirements actually get stricter than before.
Every comment now needs a delivery confirmation mechanism.
Reliable per-message delivery gives way to a collective vibe.
Public comments need to be turned into private messages.
q_en: How does the design goal change when comments arrive too fast to read one by one?
optionExplanations: 延迟要求实际上是放宽了，不是变得更严格，这个方向说反了。
逐条确认反而违背了「氛围优先」这个洞察，是加了不必要的强保证。
对，量级过高时产品目标从逐条阅读转成感知热度，采样和快照才合理。
私信是完全不同的功能形态，跟群体评论区的体验诉求无关。
optionExplanations_en: Latency requirements actually loosen, not tighten — this points the wrong direction.
Requiring per-message confirmation actually fights the 'vibe over accuracy' insight by adding an unneeded strong guarantee.
Right — at that scale the product goal shifts from reading every line to sensing crowd energy, which makes sampling and snapshots reasonable.
Private messaging is an entirely different feature and unrelated to what a shared comment section needs to deliver.
scenario: 一场超级直播峰值每秒上万条评论，一秒钟就刷过几百条，人眼根本读不完。
scenario_en: A mega live video peaks at tens of thousands of comments per second, hundreds flying by every second, far more than anyone can read.

scenario: 单场超级直播评论如洪水，观众只需要看到「足够多」的评论来感受人群能量，不需要每条都看到。
q: 第一个减负手段是？
options: 无脑加推送服务器，硬扛全量评论
直接关闭该直播的评论功能来止损
改成每分钟把这一分钟全部评论批量投递一次
对评论流做采样：每个观众只收一小部分
why: 既然没人读得完，就没必要全量投递。采样让每个观众收到可读数量的评论，同时保留现场感。
why_en: Since nobody can read them all, sampling delivers only a subset of comments to each viewer while preserving the feeling of crowd energy.
whenOtherWins: 普通流量的直播必须逐条投递——采样只在评论量超出人类阅读能力的超级流里才合理。
options_en: Blindly add push servers and brute-force the full volume.
Just turn off comments on that live video to stop the bleeding.
Switch to delivering that minute's full batch of comments once a minute.
Sample the comment stream so each viewer receives only a subset.
tradeoff: 采样保留现场感 vs 全量投递保证不丢条
q_en: What is the first way to reduce load?
scenario_en: In a super-hot live stream, comments arrive like a flood; viewers need enough comments to feel the crowd, not every single comment.
optionExplanations: 普通流量的直播必须逐条投递，加机器能扛住连接，但扛不住评论本身的消息量。
直接关闭评论是逃避问题，不是解决超量评论的负载问题。
批量投递会把延迟拖到远超实时目标，跟氛围体验的诉求也不匹配。
对，把每个观众的接收速率压到可读范围；后台仍可保留全量数据用于存档或风控。
optionExplanations_en: For a normal-volume stream, every comment still needs delivery; adding servers helps with connections but not with the sheer message volume itself.
Simply turning comments off dodges the problem instead of addressing the excess load.
Batching once a minute drags latency far past the real-time target and doesn't match the vibe experience users want.
Right — cap each viewer delivery rate at something readable, while the backend can still keep the full stream for archive or moderation.

q: 自适应采样率大概怎么调？
options: 永远固定采样 10%，完全不随流速变化
评论流速越快，采样率反而调得越高
流速越快采样率越低，维持恒定可读速率
只在流量低谷、评论很少时才开启采样
why: 采样率跟着评论速度反向调节，目标是给观众一个恒定、可读的速率，无论后台实际多快。
why_en: The sampling rate adapts inversely to comment velocity, from about fifty percent at one hundred per second down to one or two percent at five thousand, keeping each viewer's rate roughly constant.
options_en: Always sample a fixed 10%, never adjusted by velocity.
The faster comments flow, the higher the sampling rate gets.
Faster flow means lower sampling rate, keeping a steady rate.
Only enable sampling during a lull when comments are sparse.
scenario: 超级直播的采样组件要根据当前评论速度动态调整采样比例，面试官问大致怎么调。
q_en: How should adaptive sampling roughly tune its rate?
scenario_en: The sampling component for a super-hot live stream adjusts its sampling ratio based on the current comment rate.
optionExplanations: 固定不变的采样率没法跟着评论速度走，流量一涨观众照样被淹没。
方向反了：流速越快反而应该采样率越低，不是越高。
对，设定目标阅读速率 R，则采样率约等于 R / 当前评论速率；流越快，比例越低。
只在低谷才开启采样，意味着流量高峰时反而全量投递，正好搞反了触发时机。
optionExplanations_en: A fixed rate that never adjusts can't track comment velocity, so viewers still get flooded once volume spikes.
The direction is backwards: faster flow should mean a lower rate, not a higher one.
Right — if the target readable rate is R, the sample rate is roughly R divided by current comment velocity; the faster the flow, the lower the rate.
Only sampling during a lull means full delivery happens right at peak traffic — exactly backwards on when to trigger it.

q: 比纯随机更聪明的采样会优先保留哪些评论？（多选）
options: 观众所关注用户发的评论
已经获得表情互动（reactions）的评论
认证账号发的评论
字数最多的评论
why: 采样可以带策略：社交关系、互动热度、账号可信度都能加权，让「最好的」评论有更高概率被看见。字数长短不是质量信号。
why_en: Smarter sampling prioritizes comments from followed users, comments already getting reactions, and verified accounts so the best comments are more likely to be seen.
options_en: Comments from users the viewer follows.
Comments that have already gotten reactions.
Comments from verified accounts.
The longest comments by word count.
q_en: What should smarter-than-random sampling prefer to keep?
optionExplanations: 挡住的是「刷掉认识的人」这个风险：关注关系是常见的社交排序信号，让观众更可能看到熟悉的名字。
挡住的是「埋没热门评论」这个风险：已经获得互动的评论说明有共鸣，值得优先保留。
挡住的是「淹没可信来源」这个风险：认证账号自带一定可信度，可以作为排序加权项。
字数长短不是评论质量的可靠信号，按它加权反而可能优先保留水评论。
optionExplanations_en: It blocks the risk of burying people you follow: follow relationships are a common social ranking signal that surfaces familiar names.
It blocks the risk of drowning out popular comments: ones already getting reactions show resonance and deserve priority.
It blocks the risk of losing credible sources: verified accounts carry some built-in trust worth weighting in ranking.
Word count isn't a reliable quality signal — weighting by it risks surfacing padded, low-value comments instead.
scenario: 超级直播每秒上万条评论，每个观众只能收到其中约 100 条，得挑最值得看的。
scenario_en: With tens of thousands of comments per second, each viewer can only receive about a hundred, so we must keep the ones worth seeing.

q: 采样大幅减负之后，还剩下什么痛点？
options: 采样会打乱评论原本的时间先后顺序
连接成本没降：仍要维持百万级持久连接
采样率一旦设定就再也无法调整
数据库这一侧的写入压力不减反增
why: 采样只减少了每条连接上的消息量，连接本身一个都没少。百万级长连接的成本仍然存在，这为 CDN 方案留下了空间。
why_en: Sampling cuts message volume but still leaves millions of persistent SSE connections to maintain, so infrastructure costs remain substantial.
options_en: Sampling scrambles the original chronological order.
Connection cost stays: millions of persistent connections remain.
Once set, the sampling rate can never be adjusted again.
Write pressure on the database side actually increases.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: After sampling cuts message volume, what pain point remains?
optionExplanations: 采样不影响评论本身的时间戳和顺序，打乱顺序不是它留下的问题。
对，fan-out 的主计量单位仍是活跃 SSE 连接；采样降的是每连接消息数，不是连接数。
自适应采样本来就是按流速动态调整的，说「一旦设定就无法调整」与事实相反。
写路径和采样机制是完全独立的部分，采样不会让数据库写压力增加。
optionExplanations_en: Sampling doesn't touch comment timestamps or order, so scrambled ordering isn't the leftover problem.
Right — fan-out is still counted by active SSE connections; sampling lowers messages per connection, not the number of connections.
Adaptive sampling is dynamically tuned by velocity already, so claiming the rate can never change afterward is the opposite of true.
The write path and the sampling mechanism are fully independent, so sampling doesn't add database write pressure.
scenario: 采样把每条连接上的评论量从每秒上万压到几十条，但同时在线观众仍是 100 万。
scenario_en: Sampling cuts per-connection volume from tens of thousands to dozens per second, but a million viewers are still online.

scenario: 世界杯决赛级别：单流数亿观众同时在线、评论洪流不断，连采样后的 SSE 连接成本都不可承受。
q: 最具扩展性的交付模型是？
options: 把现有的采样率压得比现在更低
换成 WebSocket 集群硬扛所有连接
按地域多部署几组边缘 SSE 服务器
反转成拉模型，把快照交给 CDN 分发
why: 「把同一份内容发给千万人」正是 CDN 的本职工作。评论快照只是又一份可缓存内容，推送连接的成本被整体消除。
why_en: For mega-streams the most scalable answer is a pull model where the server snapshots recent comments to a CDN and clients poll it every second.
whenOtherWins: 中等观看量的普通直播仍应走 SSE 推送，保住 200 毫秒内的真实时体验。
diagram:
flowchart LR C["评论流"] --> RB["环形缓冲
最近100-200条"] RB -->|"每秒快照"| O["Redis / CDN 源站"] O --> E["CDN 边缘节点"] E -->|"每秒轮询"| P["数亿客户端"]
options_en: Push the existing sampling rate even lower.
Switch to a WebSocket cluster to brute-force the connections.
Deploy more region-local edge SSE server clusters.
Invert to a pull model, handing snapshots to a CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单条 TCP 连接上提供全双工双向通信的协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket provides full-duplex two-way communication over a single TCP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

tradeoff: CDN 拉模型的近乎无限扩展 vs SSE 推送的低延迟
q_en: What is the most scalable delivery model?
scenario_en: At World Cup final scale, hundreds of millions of viewers are online on one stream, and even sampled SSE connections are too expensive.
optionExplanations: 采样率再怎么压低，连接本身的数量和成本都消不掉，治标不治本。
WebSocket 每条连接的开销比 SSE 更高，换协议不能解决连接成本的问题。
按地域多部署边缘集群只是把连接总量分摊到更多机器，没有消除它。
对，反转成拉模型后，评论快照只是又一份可缓存内容，交给 CDN 分发把连接成本整体消除；中等观看量的普通直播仍该走 SSE 保住真实时体验。
optionExplanations_en: No matter how low you push the sampling rate, the connection count and its cost never actually go away — this treats the symptom, not the cause.
WebSocket costs more per connection than SSE, so swapping protocols doesn't solve the connection-cost problem.
Deploying more region-local edge clusters just spreads the same total connection load across more machines without eliminating it.

Right — flipping to a pull model turns a comment snapshot into just another cacheable asset that a CDN can distribute, eliminating connection cost entirely; a normally-sized stream should still use SSE push to keep true real-time feel.

q: CDN 快照方案里，服务端具体做什么？
options: 维护环形缓冲，定期把快照写到 CDN 源站
把每一条评论都单独实时推送到 CDN
把整场直播的全部历史评论打包上传
让 CDN 反过来代理 SSE 这类长连接
why: 环形缓冲天然只保留最近的评论窗口；周期快照把「实时流」降维成「静态可缓存内容」，正好交给 CDN 的边缘分发能力。
why_en: The server keeps a ring buffer of the last one to two hundred comments and snapshots it roughly every second to the CDN origin for global edge caching.
diagram:
graph LR
    Comments[Fast comment stream] --> Aggregator[Snapshot builder]
    Aggregator --> Object[(Latest snapshot)]
    Object --> CDN[CDN edge]
    CDN --> Clients[Clients poll every second]
options_en: Keep a ring buffer and periodically write snapshots to the CDN origin.
Push every single comment to the CDN individually.
Bundle and upload the entire video's full comment history.
Have the CDN reverse-proxy long connections like SSE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定大小、写满后从头覆盖旧数据的缓冲结构
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ring buffer is a fixed-size buffer that overwrites the oldest data once full.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

q_en: In the CDN snapshot model, what exactly does the server do?
optionExplanations: 对，服务端维护最近窗口，再按固定周期生成对象；CDN 擅长复制这种静态快照。
逐条推送到 CDN 仍是实时推送的成本，没有降维成静态内容。
打包整场历史评论跟「只保留最近窗口」的环形缓冲设计不符。
CDN 擅长的是缓存静态内容，不是代理 SSE 这类长连接。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the server keeps a recent window and periodically writes an object; the CDN is good at copying that static snapshot.
Pushing every comment individually to the CDN still carries push costs and never becomes static content.
Bundling the entire history contradicts a ring buffer that's designed to keep only a recent window.
A CDN excels at caching static content, not proxying long-lived connections like SSE.
scenario: 超级直播改用 CDN 分发评论：源站评论仍在持续产生，边缘节点只会缓存静态内容。
scenario_en: A mega stream switches to CDN delivery: the origin keeps producing comments, while edge nodes only cache static content.

q: 客户端每秒拉到一份新快照后，怎么渲染才不显得生硬？
options: 把快照里的全部评论一次性无动画地倾倒上屏
丢弃上一份快照，把整个列表重新绘制
按时间戳把新评论在轮询间隔内匀速动画播出
只显示这份快照里最新的第一条评论
why: 一次性倾倒会很跳戏。客户端把新评论摊开在轮询间隔里逐条动画，甚至按真实时间戳排布节奏，体验就像连续流。
why_en: Instead of dumping the snapshot at once, the client animates new comments smoothly across the polling interval using their timestamps to feel organic.
options_en: Dump every comment in the snapshot onto the screen at once with no animation.
Discard the previous snapshot and redraw the whole list.
Animate the new comments evenly across the polling interval using their timestamps.
Show only the newest comment in the snapshot.
q_en: How should the client render a fresh snapshot each second without feeling jumpy?
optionExplanations: 一次性把快照全部倾倒上屏会显得很跳戏，破坏连续感。
整屏重绘代价大，观感同样生硬，不比一次性上屏更好。
对，按评论真实时间戳把新内容摊开在轮询间隔里逐条动画播出，体验就像连续流。
只显示第一条丢掉了这份快照里的大部分信息，观众会漏看内容。
optionExplanations_en: Dumping the whole snapshot onto the screen at once feels jarring and breaks the sense of continuity.
Redrawing the entire list is expensive and looks just as abrupt, no better than a one-shot dump.
Right — animating new comments one by one across the polling interval, paced by their real timestamps, feels like a continuous stream.
Showing only the first comment throws away most of the snapshot, so viewers miss content.
scenario: 客户端每秒从 CDN 拉一份含最近 100 条评论的快照，两次拉取之间屏幕不能僵住。
scenario_en: The client pulls a snapshot of the last hundred comments from the CDN once a second, and the screen must not freeze in between.

q: 补全 SSE 与 CDN 模式的动态切换阈值：
text: 当单场直播超过 {{10 万}} 并发观众、或评论超过每秒 {{500}} 条时，系统自动从 {{SSE}} 推送切换为 {{CDN}} 快照拉取，客户端无缝完成过渡。
why: 阈值可以动态设定：观众数或评论速率任一越线就翻转交付模式。这两个数字是面试里值得说出口的量级。
why_en: The system automatically flips from SSE push to CDN pull when a stream crosses about one hundred thousand concurrent viewers or five hundred comments per second.
q_en: Fill in the dynamic switching thresholds between SSE and CDN mode.

q: CDN 拉模型牺牲了什么？为什么可以接受？
options: 牺牲了可用性，直播高峰期会直接拒绝服务
有一部分评论会因此永久丢失
边缘节点会趁机篡改评论的内容
换来 1-2 秒延迟，但用户本就读不过来
why: 这是一次自觉的权衡：在需求已经变质的超级流场景里，用 1-2 秒的延迟换取近乎无限的读扩展，是划算的交易。
why_en: The trade-off is one to two seconds of latency instead of sub-200 milliseconds, acceptable because users cannot engage with individual comments at that scale anyway.
options_en: Availability is sacrificed, peak traffic gets refused.
A portion of comments are permanently lost as a result.
Edge nodes tamper with comment content in the process.
Trades for 1-2s latency, but users can't read that fast anyway.
q_en: What does the CDN pull model sacrifice, and why is that acceptable?
optionExplanations: 拉模型的可用性反而更强，说牺牲可用性与事实相反。
评论仍完整持久化在数据库里，说会永久丢失与事实不符。
CDN 只是缓存分发内容，不会修改评论内容本身。
对，团队自觉接受 1-2 秒延迟换取近乎无限的读扩展，因为用户在这个量级下本就跟不上逐条阅读。
optionExplanations_en: The pull model actually has stronger availability; claiming it's sacrificed is the opposite of reality.
Comments remain fully persisted in the database, so claiming permanent loss doesn't match how it works.
A CDN only caches and distributes content — it never alters comment content itself.
Right — the team consciously trades 1-2 seconds of latency for near-limitless read scale, since users can't keep up with reading every comment at this volume anyway.
scenario: 超级直播改成每秒一份 CDN 快照轮询，读扩展几乎无限，但快照有生成与缓存周期。
scenario_en: A mega stream moves to one CDN snapshot per second: read scaling is nearly unlimited, but snapshots have a build and cache cycle.

q: CDN 轮询有 1-2 秒延迟，但我发的评论想立刻看到（read-your-own-write），怎么办？
options: 给发评论的人临时单独开一条 SSE 连接
发完评论后强制客户端立即多轮询一次 CDN
提示用户等一两秒再手动刷新页面
客户端乐观插入：自己的评论立即上屏，与轮询解耦
why: 读己之写在客户端本地解决最便宜：发出去的评论直接插进自己的 feed，别人晚一秒看到无所谓。
why_en: The client optimistically inserts the user's own comment into their feed immediately, independent of the CDN polling cycle.
options_en: Open a dedicated SSE connection just for the person commenting.
Force the client to poll the CDN one extra time right after posting.
Tell the user to wait a second or two and refresh manually.
Optimistic local insert: the user's own comment shows instantly, decoupled from polling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保证用户能立刻看到自己刚写入的数据
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-your-own-writes guarantees a user immediately sees data they just wrote.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

q_en: With 1-2 seconds of CDN polling delay, how do I see my own comment immediately?
optionExplanations: 为发言用户单独开 SSE 连接又背上了长连接成本，跟避免连接开销的初衷相反。
额外轮询一次仍受 CDN 缓存刷新周期限制，不能保证立即可见。
让用户被动等待仍然是糟糕体验，没有真正解决问题。
对，发出去的评论直接在本地插进自己的 feed，跟 CDN 轮询完全解耦，零延迟且实现简单。
optionExplanations_en: Opening a dedicated SSE connection just for the poster reintroduces the exact connection cost being avoided.
One extra poll still runs into the CDN's own cache refresh cycle, so it can't guarantee instant visibility.
Making the user passively wait is still a poor experience and doesn't actually solve the problem.
Right — the client inserts the posted comment straight into its own feed locally, fully decoupled from CDN polling, zero latency and simple to build.
scenario: 已切到 1-2 秒延迟的 CDN 快照轮询，但观众点下发送后必须立刻在屏幕上看到自己的评论。
scenario_en: We are on CDN snapshot polling with one to two seconds of lag, yet a viewer must see their own comment the instant they hit send.

q: 观看人数在切换阈值附近来回徘徊会发生什么？怎么治？
options: 两种模式反复抖动，需要给阈值加上滞回
没有任何影响，模式切换本身是免费的
客户端会因为模式切换直接崩溃退出
CDN 上的缓存会被这次切换全部清空
why: 单一阈值在临界点附近会导致高频模式翻转，每次切换都有成本。滞回让「升级」和「降级」的门限拉开距离，抖动自然消失。
why_en: Viewership hovering near the cutoff causes flapping between modes, so the threshold logic needs hysteresis with separate up and down triggers.
options_en: The two modes flap back and forth, so add hysteresis to the threshold.
There's no impact at all — switching modes is free.
The client crashes outright because of the mode switch.
CDN caches get completely wiped by the switch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给状态切换设置不同的上下门限，防止在临界点反复抖动
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hysteresis uses different up and down thresholds to prevent flapping near a boundary.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

q_en: What happens near a switching threshold, and how do we fix it?
optionExplanations: 对，观看人数在阈值附近徘徊会让两种模式反复翻转，每次切换都有成本，加上滞回让升级和降级门限拉开距离才能消除抖动。
每次模式切换都有连接建立/断开的成本，说完全没影响不成立。
模式切换只影响交付路径，不会导致客户端直接崩溃。
CDN 缓存和交付模式切换是两套独立机制，切换不会清空缓存。
optionExplanations_en: Right — viewership hovering near the cutoff flips the two modes back and forth, and every switch has a cost, so hysteresis with separate up/down thresholds is what stops the flapping.
Every mode switch carries connection setup/teardown cost, so claiming zero impact doesn't hold.
A mode switch only affects the delivery path; it doesn't crash the client outright.
CDN caching and delivery-mode switching are independent mechanisms, so switching doesn't wipe the cache.
scenario: 系统按在线人数在 SSE 推送和 CDN 快照两种模式间切换，某场直播人数正好在阈值上下波动。
scenario_en: The system flips between SSE push and CDN snapshots based on viewer count, and one video hovers right around the threshold.

q: 为什么说 CDN 快照方案「优雅」？
options: 因为 CDN 边缘带宽便宜，可以随便用不用心疼成本
快照只是又一份可缓存内容，交还给 CDN 天然强项
因为 CDN 能为评论提供强一致性保证
因为 CDN 会自动帮我们把评论做采样
why: 优雅在于问题重构：不再造更大的推送系统，而是把实时流降维成静态内容，套进现成的、已被验证的分发管道。
why_en: It is elegant because a comment snapshot becomes just another piece of cacheable content served by infrastructure that already exists for exactly this job.
options_en: Because CDN edge bandwidth is cheap, so you can use it freely without worrying about cost.
A snapshot is just cacheable content, handed to the CDN's natural strength.
Because CDNs provide strong consistency guarantees for comments.
Because CDNs automatically do comment sampling for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

q_en: Why is the CDN snapshot approach considered elegant?
optionExplanations: 便宜与否是成本问题，不是「优雅」这个词想表达的重构含义。
对，优雅在于把实时流降维成又一份静态可缓存内容，直接套进 CDN 已经验证过的分发管道，不用再造一个更大的推送系统。
CDN 提供的是最终一致的边缘缓存，不是强一致性保证。
采样发生在服务端生成快照之前，CDN 只负责分发，不做采样。
optionExplanations_en: Whether bandwidth is cheap is a cost question, not what 'elegant' is pointing at here — the reframing.

Right — the elegance is turning a real-time stream into just another piece of static, cacheable content that slots into a CDN's already-proven delivery pipeline instead of building a bigger push system.
A CDN offers eventually-consistent edge caching, not a strong consistency guarantee.
Sampling happens server-side before the snapshot is built; the CDN only distributes it and does no sampling.
scenario: 超级直播的评论分发已降维成每秒一份静态快照，公司现成的 CDN 边缘节点遍布全球。
scenario_en: Mega-stream comment delivery is now one static snapshot per second, and the company already has CDN edges worldwide.

q: 在面试信号上，采样方案和 CDN 快照方案分别代表什么水平？
options: 两者都是及格线要求，谈了也没有区分度
CDN 快照其实是错误答案，面试里不该提出来
采样是理解，CDN 快照是 staff 级信号
采样太简单，面试里提了反而扣分
why: 区分度在于洞察层级：采样是聪明的优化，CDN 方案是对问题的重新定义。能说出「需求在极端规模下变质」这句话本身就是信号。
why_en: Discussing sampling shows strong understanding, while the CDN approach signals staff-level thinking because it recognizes that the requirements themselves change at extreme scale.
options_en: Both are baseline expectations and carry no differentiating signal.
The CDN snapshot is actually the wrong answer and shouldn't be raised in an interview.
Sampling shows understanding; the CDN snapshot is a staff-level signal.
Sampling is so simple that raising it actually costs you points.
q_en: What interview signal do sampling and CDN snapshots each show?
optionExplanations: 两者其实是分层信号，不是同一条及格线，这个说法低估了区分度。
CDN 方案是本题的高分方向，不是错误答案。
对，采样说明你会降负载；快照说明你看出极端流量下产品目标已经变了。
采样方案本身也展示了对负载问题的扎实理解，不该被跳过。
optionExplanations_en: The two actually sit at different levels, not the same bar — this underrates how much they differentiate.
The CDN approach is the higher-scoring direction here, not a wrong answer.
Right — sampling shows you can reduce load; snapshots show you noticed the product goal changes under extreme traffic.
Sampling itself already demonstrates solid understanding of the load problem and shouldn't be skipped.
scenario: 面试最后 10 分钟，面试官问「峰值再涨 10 倍怎么办」，你可以谈采样也可以谈 CDN 快照。
scenario_en: In the last ten minutes the interviewer asks what happens if peak traffic grows tenfold; you can talk sampling or CDN snapshots.

q: 把「超级直播评论交付」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 代价：评论延迟升到 1-2 秒
需求：世界杯级单流——数亿观众、每秒数千条评论
缓解：自己的评论本地乐观插入；切换阈值加滞回防抖动
选型：每秒快照环形缓冲，经 CDN 分发，客户端轮询拉取
洞察：没人读得过来，「逐条实时送达」这个需求本身已失效
why: 链条是：极端规模需求 → 认识到需求变质 → 反转为 CDN 拉模型 → 付出 1-2 秒延迟 → 用乐观插入和滞回把体验补齐。
why_en: The chain runs from mega-scale demand to the insight that per-comment delivery no longer matters, leading to CDN snapshots, a latency cost, and mitigations like optimistic inserts and hysteresis.
diagram:
graph TD
    Normal[SSE per viewer] --> Hot{Huge live?}
    Hot -->|no| SSE[Continue SSE]
    Hot -->|yes| Sample[Sample comments]
    Sample --> CDN[CDN snapshot pull]
q_en: Put the super-live comment delivery decision chain in the right order.

q: 把「评论实时推送技术选型」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 关键属性：读写极不均衡——绝大多数观众只读不发
代价：代理可能缓冲流式响应、浏览器限制每域 SSE 连接数
需求：新评论要在 200 毫秒内送达所有观众
选型：SSE 单向推流；发评论仍走普通 HTTP POST
排除轮询：要近实时就得毫秒级轮询，数据库扛不住且大多空查
why: 从延迟需求出发，排除轮询、抓住读写不均衡这个决定性属性，落到 SSE，最后正视它的基础设施代价。
why_en: Starting from the latency requirement you rule out polling, use the read-heavy imbalance to pick SSE over WebSockets, and then face its proxy and browser-limit costs.
q_en: Put the live-comment push technology decision chain in the right order.

q: 把「跨服务器评论分发」的决策链排成正确顺序：
steps: 缓解：L7 负载均衡按 liveVideoId 一致性哈希，把同一视频的观众聚到同一台服务器
需求：百万级并发观众，单机长连接不够用，必须横向扩展推送服务器
选型：pub/sub 广播新评论，并用 hash(liveVideoId) % N 分频道控制频道数量
代价：round-robin 让每台服务器观众混杂，被迫订阅大量频道
问题：同一视频的观众连在不同服务器上，收到评论的那台送不到其他台的观众
why: 横向扩展引出跨服务器送达问题，pub/sub + 分频道解决通知，round-robin 暴露订阅膨胀的代价，最后靠 L7 协同定位收口。
why_en: Horizontal scaling creates the cross-server delivery problem, sharded pub/sub solves notification, round-robin exposes subscription bloat, and layer-7 co-location fixes it.
q_en: Put the cross-server comment distribution decision chain in the right order.

q: 断线重连时「什么都不做、只收之后的新评论」，代价是什么？
options: 服务器会因此发生内存泄漏问题
重连过程必然会因此彻底失败
评论会因此重复显示两遍给用户
断线期间的评论会对用户永久丢失
why: 移动网络天生不稳，用户切后台、进隧道、换网络是常态。不做补漏，每次抖动都是一次糟糕体验。
why_en: Doing nothing means comments posted during a disconnect are simply lost, so even a five-second WiFi hiccup makes users miss all the reactions to a big moment.
options_en: It causes a memory leak on the server.
Reconnection is bound to fail outright as a result.
Comments end up displayed twice to the user.
Comments posted during the disconnect are permanently lost to that user.
q_en: What is the cost of doing nothing on reconnect and only receiving future comments?
optionExplanations: 内存泄漏和是否补漏是两回事，跟断线策略没有因果关系。
重连本身仍能正常建立，问题不在连接能不能重新建起来。
什么都不做只会遗漏，不会造成重复，这个说法方向反了。
对，断线期间发生的评论对这个用户就是永久丢失了，移动网络下抖动是常态，每次都是一次糟糕体验。
optionExplanations_en: A memory leak and whether gaps get backfilled are unrelated — no causal link to the disconnect strategy.
Reconnection itself still succeeds fine; the problem isn't whether the connection can come back up.
Doing nothing only causes omissions, not duplicates — this points the wrong direction.
Right — comments posted during the gap are permanently lost to that user; mobile networks flake constantly, so every hiccup becomes a bad experience.
scenario: 移动端观众进电梯掉线 15 秒后重连，这期间直播评论区一直在产出新评论。
scenario_en: A mobile viewer drops for fifteen seconds in an elevator and reconnects, while the stream kept producing comments the whole time.

q: SSE（服务器推流协议）内建的断线补漏机制怎么运作？
options: 服务器为每个会话缓存全部发过的内容，重连时整段重发
客户端每隔一段时间做一次全量拉取来兜底
事件带唯一 ID，靠 Last-Event-ID 重放缺口
完全依赖 TCP 层的自动重传补齐，应用层什么都不用管
why: 这是 SSE 相对 WebSocket 的隐藏优势：协议原生定义了事件 ID 与 Last-Event-ID 重连语义，浏览器自动执行，服务端只需实现重放。
why_en: Every SSE event carries an id, and on reconnect the browser automatically sends the Last-Event-ID header so the server can replay missed comments before resuming the stream.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant S as 推送服务器
    C->>S: 重连 + Last-Event-ID: c_1088
    S->>C: 重放 c_1089 … c_1095（漏掉的）
    S->>C: 接回实时流
options_en: The server caches everything it ever sent per session and resends the whole thing on reconnect.
The client periodically does a full pull as a fallback.
Each event carries a unique id, and Last-Event-ID replays the gap.
It relies entirely on TCP-level retransmission to fill the gap, with nothing at the application layer.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a connection-oriented transport protocol that guarantees ordered, reliable delivery.

q_en: How does SSE natively fill gaps after a disconnect?
optionExplanations: 缓存每个会话的全部历史成本会失控，只需要保留近期窗口就够。
客户端定期全量拉取等于退化回轮询，丢掉了 SSE 原生补漏的优势。
对，浏览器重连时自动带上收到过的最后一个事件 ID，服务器据此定位缺口只补发遗漏部分。
TCP 只保证已建立连接内的可靠传输，补不回连接断开期间发生的应用层消息。
optionExplanations_en: Caching every piece of every session's history would spiral in cost; keeping only a recent window is enough.
Having the client periodically pull everything degrades back into polling and loses SSE's native gap-fill advantage.
Right — on reconnect the browser automatically resends the id of the last event it saw, and the server uses it to locate and replay just the missing part.
TCP only guarantees reliable delivery within an established connection; it can't recover application-level messages from while the connection was down.
scenario: SSE 客户端断线后重连，服务端在共享缓存里留有最近几分钟的评论，可按 ID 定位。
scenario_en: An SSE client reconnects after a drop, and the server keeps the last few minutes of comments in a shared cache addressable by id.

q: 读这次重连交互，服务器看到 Last-Event-ID: c_1088 后在做什么？
codeSample:
GET /comments/stream/lv_42 HTTP/1.1
Accept: text/event-stream
Last-Event-ID: c_1088

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream

id: c_1089
data: {"message":"what a play!"}

id: c_1090
data: {"message":"unreal"}
options: 从这场直播最开始的评论全量推送
重置连接，并要求客户端重新鉴权
直接忽略这个头，只发后续新评论
从缺口开始重放，再无缝接回实时流
why: Last-Event-ID 就是客户端的断点书签：服务器按它定位缺口、补发缺失的评论，然后继续正常流式推送。
why_en: Seeing the Last-Event-ID header, the server replays the comments the client missed after that id and then resumes normal live streaming.
options_en: Push every comment from the very start of the live video.
Reset the connection and force the client to re-authenticate.
Just ignore the header and only send new comments going forward.
Replay from the gap, then seamlessly resume the live stream.

q_en: In this reconnect flow, what does the server do after seeing Last-Event-ID: c_1088?
optionExplanations: 只需要补发缺失的那一段，从头全量推送会重复浪费带宽。
这个头只表示客户端最后看到哪里；身份仍由鉴权层处理。
忽略这个头会让客户端彻底错过断线期间的评论，等于没有补漏。
对，服务器按这个 ID 定位缺口、补发遗漏的评论，再无缝切回正常的实时推送。
optionExplanations_en: Only the missing segment needs replaying; pushing the entire history from scratch wastes bandwidth on duplicates.
That header only tells where the client last stopped; identity is still handled by the auth layer.
Ignoring the header means the client misses everything from the outage entirely, which defeats the point of catch-up.
Right — the server uses that id to locate the gap, replays the missed comments, and then seamlessly resumes normal live push.
scenario: 客户端断线后重连，浏览器 EventSource 自动带上了它收到的最后一条评论 ID。
scenario_en: The client reconnects after a drop and the browser EventSource automatically carries the last comment id it received.

scenario: 想在重连时做更精细的 UX——比如显示「你错过了 47 条评论」、以 2-3 倍速平滑补播——而不是依赖浏览器默默续传。
q: 客户端该怎么做？
options: 只依赖浏览器原生的 Last-Event-ID 机制
本地记录最后见到的评论 ID，重连时显式 GET 补齐
重连时直接刷新整个页面重来
让服务器为每个用户持久保存断点位置
why: 自己掌握断点和补课请求，就能自由设计重连体验：倍速动画补播、跳到实况的选项等。浏览器自动续传做不到这些。
why_en: Tracking the last comment id locally and requesting catch-up over explicit HTTP gives the client full control to animate missed comments or offer a jump-to-live option.
whenOtherWins: 简单 Web 客户端没有特殊 UX 要求时，浏览器原生 Last-Event-ID 自动续传就足够了。
options_en: Rely solely on the browser's native Last-Event-ID mechanism.
Track the last seen comment id locally and explicitly GET the backfill on reconnect.
Just refresh the whole page when reconnecting.
Have the server persist each user's resume position.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-Event-ID is the SSE header the client resends on reconnect so the server can replay missed events.

tradeoff: 客户端自控断点 vs 浏览器原生自动续传
q_en: What should the client do for a more controlled reconnect experience?
scenario_en: You want a refined reconnect UX, such as showing “you missed 47 comments” and replaying them at 2-3x speed, instead of relying on silent browser retry.
optionExplanations: 没有特殊 UX 要求的简单客户端，浏览器原生自动续传其实够用；但想要倍速动画补播这类定制体验就做不到。
对，客户端自己记住最后见到的评论 ID，重连时显式发 GET 请求补历史，就能自由设计倍速动画、跳到实况等体验。
整页刷新会打断观看状态，体验比针对性补课差很多。
断点该由客户端掌握，让服务端为每个用户存一份位置是不必要的额外状态。
optionExplanations_en: For a simple client with no special UX needs, the browser's native auto-resume is genuinely enough; it just can't do custom things like sped-up replay animation.
Right — the client tracks the last seen comment id itself and fires an explicit GET on reconnect to backfill, which frees it to design fast-forward playback or a jump-to-live option.
A full page refresh breaks the viewing state and is a much worse experience than a targeted catch-up.
The resume point belongs on the client; having the server persist a position per user is unnecessary extra state.

q: 移动端为兼顾电量，SSE（服务器推流）长连接该怎么管理？
options: 退到后台后也始终保持连接不断开
后台期间改用推送通知逐条发送评论
退后台前主动断开，回前台再补课
认为移动端只能靠轮询来实现
why: 与其让系统强制掐断，不如主动优雅断开并记好书签。省电、省资源，回前台后靠追赶机制无损恢复。
why_en: The app preemptively disconnects the SSE and records its position when backgrounded, then reconnects and catches up on foreground, which beats keeping a throttled background connection.
options_en: Keep the connection alive even when backgrounded.
Switch to sending each comment as a push notification while backgrounded.
Proactively disconnect before backgrounding, catch up on foreground.
Assume mobile can only be implemented with polling.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

q_en: How should mobile clients manage SSE long connections to save battery?
optionExplanations: 后台常开连接正是耗电的来源，跟省电的目标相反。
逐条推送通知在评论量大的直播下会变成骚扰式轰炸，不适合这个场景。
对，后台前保存最后评论 ID 并关连接；回到前台后用追赶接口补齐缺口。
SSE 同样能在移动端正常工作，不是只能靠轮询实现。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the connection alive in the background is exactly what drains battery, the opposite of the goal.
Sending each comment as a push notification would turn into a barrage during a busy live stream, a bad fit here.
Right — save the last comment id before backgrounding, close the connection, and use catch-up on foreground to fill the gap.
SSE works fine on mobile too; it isn't limited to polling.
scenario: 手机用户把直播切到后台只听声音，系统几分钟后会回收网络连接，电量还在掉。
scenario_en: A phone user backgrounds the stream to keep listening; the OS reclaims network connections after a few minutes and the battery keeps draining.

q: 断线补漏的重放范围该设多大边界？
options: 重放最近约 5 分钟，超出边界则优雅降级
无论断开多久都从直播开头做一次全量重放
只补最后 1 条评论就已经足够
永不重放，重连即代表只看最新
why: 重放要有实际上限：短断线无缝补齐，长断线补太多反而淹没用户。5 分钟是一个合理的量级锚点。
why_en: Replay must be bounded, with about the last five minutes being reasonable and graceful degradation for longer gaps instead of dumping thousands of stale comments.
options_en: Replay roughly the last five minutes and degrade gracefully beyond that.
Always replay everything from the start of the video no matter how long the disconnect was.
Replaying just the single last comment is enough.
Never replay; reconnecting means you only see what comes next.
scenario: 用户断线重连后要补发错过的评论，面试官问重放范围该设多大边界。
q_en: What boundary should we set for replaying missed comments?
scenario_en: After a reconnect, the system must replay missed comments, and the interviewer asks where to bound that replay window.
optionExplanations: 对，把短中断当连续体验处理；超过窗口就给摘要或跳到最新，避免旧评论倾倒。
断多久都全量重放，长时间掉线会一次性倾倒海量旧评论，体验反而更差。
只补最后 1 条会让用户漏掉断线期间的大部分讨论，补漏形同虚设。
完全不重放会让用户直接错过断线期间的全部评论，没有兜底。
optionExplanations_en: Right — treat short outages as continuous playback; beyond the window, summarize or jump live instead of dumping stale comments.
Replaying everything regardless of gap length would dump a huge pile of stale comments on someone who was offline a long time — worse, not better.
Replaying only the single last comment leaves the user missing most of the discussion, making catch-up nearly pointless.
Never replaying at all means the user simply loses everything from the outage, with no safety net.

q: 重连大概率被负载均衡到另一台推送服务器，重放漏掉的评论靠什么？
options: 由原来那台服务器负责把断线期间的历史转发过来
客户端在本地保存全量的评论历史
断线时把用户锁定在原来那台服务器
共享缓存保存近期评论，任何服务器都能重放
why: 重放能力不能绑死在单台机器的内存里。把近期评论放进共享 Redis，重连落到哪台都能补课。
why_en: A shared Redis cache of recent comments lets whichever server the client reconnects to replay the missed history for any video.
options_en: The originally connected server forwards the missed history.
The client stores the full comment history locally.
Pin the user to the original server during disconnect.
A shared cache holds recent comments so any server can replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存型键值存储，也提供轻量的 pub/sub 广播
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store that also offers lightweight pub/sub messaging.

q_en: If reconnect lands on another push server, what replays the missed comments?
optionExplanations: 重连大概率被均衡到别的机器，原服务器未必还在或还认识这个用户。
让客户端保存全量历史既不现实也不可靠，成本远高于服务端集中处理。
把用户锁定在原服务器违背了负载均衡分散连接的初衷。
对，把近期评论放进共享的 Redis 缓存，重连落到哪台推送服务器都能查到并补齐历史。
optionExplanations_en: Reconnects are likely rebalanced to a different machine, and the original server may no longer be reachable or even remember the user.
Having the client store the full history locally is neither practical nor reliable, and far pricier than centralizing it server-side.
Pinning the user back to the original server defeats the point of load balancing spreading connections around.
Right — recent comments live in a shared Redis cache, so whichever push server the reconnect lands on can look them up and replay history.
scenario: 客户端重连时被负载均衡分到另一台推送服务器，新机器内存里没有它断线期间的评论。
scenario_en: On reconnect the load balancer lands the client on a different push server whose memory holds none of the comments it missed.

q: HTTP 补课响应还在处理时，SSE（服务器推流）连接上又来了新评论，怎么避免重复或漏洞？
options: 直接丢弃 SSE 流送来的那部分评论
按评论 ID 去重，合并两条通道的数据
让 SSE 连接在补课期间暂停接收
认为两路数据天然不会重叠，无需处理
why: 两条通道并行时窗口重叠不可避免。评论 ID 是天然的去重键，客户端据此合并即可既不重复也不缺失。
why_en: When SSE and HTTP catch-up overlap, the client deduplicates by comment id and merges the two streams correctly.
options_en: Just drop whatever the SSE stream delivers during that window.
Deduplicate by comment id and merge the two channels.
Pause the SSE connection while catch-up is in progress.
Assume the two paths never overlap, so nothing needs handling.
q_en: How do we avoid duplicates or gaps when HTTP catch-up and SSE new events overlap?
optionExplanations: 直接丢弃 SSE 送来的那部分会漏掉真正实时到达的新评论。
对，客户端维护 seenCommentIds 集合，HTTP 返回和 SSE 新事件都先查集合再插入。
暂停 SSE 接收只是把缺口从「补课前」挪到「补课中」，问题没有消失。
两条通道并行工作，重叠窗口是真实存在的，不处理会导致重复或遗漏。
optionExplanations_en: Simply dropping whatever SSE delivers during that window loses genuinely new comments arriving in real time.
Right — keep a seenCommentIds set on the client and check it before inserting data from either HTTP catch-up or SSE.
Pausing SSE reception just moves the gap from before catch-up to during it — the problem doesn't disappear.
The two channels run in parallel, so overlap genuinely happens; ignoring it causes duplicates or gaps.
scenario: 重连后客户端同时开着两路：HTTP 补课请求在返回缺口评论，SSE 流已开始推新评论。
scenario_en: After reconnecting the client runs two paths at once: an HTTP catch-up returning the gap while the SSE stream already pushes new comments.

q: 补全生产级断线处理的要点：
text: 面试谈断线处理：以 SSE 的 {{Last-Event-ID}} 机制为基础，但生产系统还需要{{有界}}重放（不能补一小时的评论）、客户端本地跟踪{{位置}}、以及无法重放时的优雅{{降级}}。

把大部分时间花在广度铺陈上，跟 staff+ 该有的广深比正好相反。

q: FB Live Comments 练的「实时更新模式」还适用于哪些系统？
options: 每天夜里批量跑一次的离线结算 ETL 数据管道

why_en: The same real-time updates pattern of streaming delivery, pub/sub distribution, and server coordination applies to collaborative editing, live dashboards, and gaming.
options_en: A nightly offline batch settlement ETL pipeline that runs once a day.
Collaborative editing, dashboards, and games that need instant delivery.
Cold data archival in object storage.
A statistics report generated once a month.
q_en: What other systems use the realtime update pattern from FB Live Comments?
optionExplanations: 夜间批量结算是延迟不敏感的批处理场景，不需要实时推送这套模式。
对，协作编辑、看板和游戏都要求事件产生后立刻 fan-out 给相关在线客户端。
冷数据归档不涉及向在线客户端实时分发，用不上这套模式。
月度报表是低频批处理，不需要毫秒级或秒级的送达保证。
optionExplanations_en: Nightly batch settlement is a latency-insensitive batch job that doesn't need this real-time push pattern.
Right — collaborative editing, dashboards, and games all need each event fanned out immediately to the relevant online clients.
Cold data archival doesn't involve real-time distribution to online clients, so this pattern doesn't apply.
A monthly report is low-frequency batch work with no need for millisecond- or second-level delivery guarantees.
scenario: 你要把这套 SSE 广播 + pub/sub 分频道 + 多机协调的骨架，迁移到另一类系统上。
scenario_en: You want to carry this skeleton — SSE broadcast, sharded pub/sub, multi-server coordination — over to a different kind of system.

q: cursor 分页仍留下的短板是什么？
options: 翻页途中插入或删除评论会让光标错位，读到重复或缺失的评论
每翻一页仍要打一次数据库查询，高流量下这批查询量本身就吃紧
光标要逐行扫过它前面的所有评论，行数越多越慢
光标字段建不了索引，查询只能退化成全表扫描
why: 文章明说 cursor 比 offset 已经省掉了扫行，但没消灭「每页一次查询」——在我们这种每秒上千评论的环境里，光这批查询量本身就是负担。要再省只能在 Realtime 层加缓存或改推送，而不是继续查库。
why_en: Cursor pagination still issues one database query per page; the article notes this is significant in our high-traffic setting, so further savings must come from caching or push, not more queries.
options_en: Inserting or deleting a comment mid-scroll shifts the cursor, causing duplicates or gaps.
It still hits the database once per page, and that query volume itself is heavy under high traffic.
The cursor must scan row by row through every comment before it, getting slower as rows grow.
The cursor field cannot be indexed, so every query degrades into a full table scan.
q_en: What limitation does cursor pagination still leave?
optionExplanations: 这是 offset 分页的毛病；cursor 恰恰是稳定的，插入删除不影响光标位置。
对，cursor 省的是扫行，不是查询次数——每一页仍要落一次库，高流量下总查询量可观。
逐行扫过前面所有行是 offset 的代价；cursor 建了索引就能直接定位，不必扫。
文章明说在光标字段上建了索引，查询按 commentId 范围直接定位，不会全表扫描。
optionExplanations_en: That's the offset pagination flaw; cursor is stable, so inserts and deletes don't shift its position.
Right — cursor saves the row scan, not the query count, so each page still costs one DB query, heavy at high volume.
Scanning every preceding row is the offset cost; with an index the cursor seeks directly instead of scanning.
The article builds an index on the cursor field, so the query seeks by commentId range rather than scanning the whole table.

termDefinitions.meaning: cursor pagination，用上一页末条记录的 id 作为下一页起点，避免扫过前面的行
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination uses the last item id of a page as the start of the next, avoiding scanning preceding rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: offset pagination，用「跳过前 N 行」定位起点，行多时要逐行数过去
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset pagination locates the start by skipping N rows, counting through every preceding row as data grows.

scenario: cursor 分页已经替掉了 offset：一个火爆直播每秒上千条评论，无数观众在无限滚动里往回翻历史评论。
scenario_en: Cursor pagination has replaced offset: a hot live video gets thousands of comments per second while countless viewers infinite-scroll back through history.

q: 想要比一致性哈希更灵活的路由，映射存在哪里？
options: 把 liveVideoId→服务器 映射只留在每台服务器各自的本地内存里，彼此从不同步
用 Zookeeper 存动态的 liveVideoId→服务器 映射，路由更灵活
用 L4 负载均衡按源 IP 哈希转发，四层不看应用信息
把映射硬编码进客户端配置，靠发版来更新
why: L7 一致性哈希是隐式规则、零额外基础设施；但要支持按负载等动态路由，就得把 liveVideoId→服务器 映射显式放进 Zookeeper 这类协调服务。代价：多了一套要运维、要保持一致的协调组件。
why_en: Consistent hashing is an implicit, zero-infrastructure rule, but a dynamic mapping in Zookeeper buys flexible routing at the cost of running and keeping a coordination service consistent.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需把同一视频的观众聚到同一台机器、不需要按负载等动态规则，L7 一致性哈希更省事，不必引入 Zookeeper。
options_en: Keep the liveVideoId→server map only in each server's local memory, unsynchronized.
Store a dynamic liveVideoId→server map in Zookeeper, buying more flexible routing.
Use an L4 load balancer hashing on source IP, which cannot see application data.
Hardcode the mapping into client config and update it via app releases.
q_en: Where do you store the mapping for routing more flexible than consistent hashing?
optionExplanations: 各机独立本地映射没有单一真相，机器增减时谁也不知道该改哪份，路由会打架。
对，动态映射放进 Zookeeper 后可以加负载感知等规则，代价是协调服务的运维复杂度。
L4 只看 IP/端口，看不见 liveVideoId，做不到「同一视频聚一台」的应用层路由。
硬编码在客户端无法随观众和机器实时变化，服务器一扩缩容映射就过期。
optionExplanations_en: Independent local maps have no single source of truth, so scaling servers leaves no one knowing which copy to fix and routes conflict.
Right — a dynamic map in Zookeeper enables rules like load-awareness, at the cost of the coordination service's operational complexity.
L4 sees only IP and port, not liveVideoId, so it cannot do the application-layer routing that co-locates a video's viewers.
A hardcoded client map cannot track live viewer and server churn, so it goes stale the moment servers scale up or down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式协调服务，用来存放并同步集群共享的元数据（如映射、配置、成员关系）
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zookeeper is a distributed coordination service that stores and synchronizes cluster-shared metadata like mappings, config, and membership.

termDefinitions.meaning: Layer 7 consistent hashing，负载均衡在应用层按 liveVideoId 哈希，把同一视频的观众稳定路由到同一台服务器
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 7 consistent hashing has the load balancer hash on liveVideoId at the application layer to route a video's viewers to the same server.

termDefinitions.meaning: Layer 4 负载均衡，只按 IP/端口等传输层信息转发，看不到应用层内容
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L4 load balancer forwards using only transport-layer info like IP and port, blind to application content.

tradeoff: L7 一致性哈希的零运维 vs Zookeeper 动态映射的灵活性
scenario: 你要把同一直播的观众聚到同一台 Realtime 服务器好收敛 pub/sub 订阅。L7 一致性哈希能做，但你还想按服务器负载等规则动态调整路由。
scenario_en: You want a video's viewers co-located on one Realtime server to shrink pub/sub subscriptions; consistent hashing works, but you also want to route dynamically by rules like server load.

q: Dispatcher 怎么知道某台推送服务器没了、别再往它转发？
options: Dispatcher 每次转发评论前先逐台 ping 所有服务器确认存活
靠心跳加注册协议：服务器上线时注册、持续心跳，心跳超时即从映射摘除
等客户端重连报错，再由客户端通知 Dispatcher 这台机器换了
固定长周期全量重建映射，宕机的机器要等下个周期才被清掉
why: 服务器上线向 Dispatcher 注册并持续心跳；宕机后心跳超时，就把它从映射摘除、评论不再投给它，观众重连转到别的机器。代价：检测窗口内的评论可能丢，靠持久化加 catch-up 补。
why_en: Servers register their videos and heartbeat on join; when one dies the heartbeat stops, the dispatcher times it out and evicts it from the map so new comments stop going there and reconnecting viewers land elsewhere.
options_en: The dispatcher pings every server to confirm liveness before forwarding each comment.
Via heartbeat plus a registration protocol: servers register on join, heartbeat continuously, and are evicted from the map on timeout.
It waits for a client reconnect error, then the client tells the dispatcher the server changed.
It rebuilds the whole map on a long fixed cycle, so a crashed server lingers until the next cycle.
q_en: How does the dispatcher learn a push server is gone and stop forwarding to it?
optionExplanations: 每条评论前 ping 全体服务器代价爆炸，且仍有 ping 后即宕的窗口，不如让服务器主动心跳。
对，注册管上线、心跳管存活：心跳超时就主动摘除路由，而不是等转发失败才发现服务器已经不在。
把探活责任推给客户端，反馈慢且不可靠，宕机到客户端报错之间评论一直投给死机。
长周期全量重建让宕机机器长时间留在映射里，其间评论持续投给死掉的服务器。
optionExplanations_en: Pinging all servers before each comment is prohibitively costly and still leaves a ping-then-die window; server-pushed heartbeats are better.
Right — registration handles join and heartbeat handles liveness, so a timeout actively evicts the route instead of discovering the gone server only after a failed forward.
Pushing liveness detection to clients is slow and unreliable, and comments keep going to the dead server until a client errors.
A long full-rebuild cycle leaves a crashed server in the map for a long time, and comments keep flowing to the dead server meanwhile.

termDefinitions.meaning: heartbeat，服务器周期性发出的存活信号，一段时间收不到就判定它下线
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a periodic liveness signal from a server; missing it for a while marks the server as down.

termDefinitions.meaning: registration protocol，服务器上线时向协调方登记自己身份与职责的约定流程
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A registration protocol is the agreed flow by which a server, on startup, registers its identity and responsibilities with the coordinator.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调度服务，维护「哪台服务器负责哪个视频」的映射，直接把新评论转发到对应服务器
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Dispatcher is a routing service that keeps a map of which server owns which video and forwards each new comment to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 补漏机制，客户端重连后按最后收到的评论 id 拉取断连期间错过的评论
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Catch-up is the recovery mechanism where a reconnecting client fetches comments it missed since its last received comment id.

scenario: Dispatcher 直接把新评论转发给「负责该视频」的 Realtime 服务器。一台 Realtime 服务器突然宕机，它名下还挂着一批正在看的观众。
scenario_en: The dispatcher forwards each new comment to the Realtime server that owns that video. One Realtime server suddenly crashes while still holding a batch of active viewers.

q: 客户端从 SSE 切到 CDN 轮询时，靠什么保证不漏评论也不重复？
options: 切换瞬间就把当前屏幕上的所有评论全部清空，再从最新一份 CDN 快照里重新拉全部内容重建整个 feed
首份 CDN 快照本就含最近 100-200 条评论，与 SSE 尾部重叠，客户端按 id 去重
断开 SSE 后先等几秒再开始拉 CDN，给服务端时间准备好快照
弹窗提示用户手动刷新页面来载入 CDN 数据
why: SSE 推时客户端记着最后评论 id；翻到 CDN 后首份快照是最近 100-200 条的环形缓冲，与 SSE 尾部重叠，按 id 去重即不漏不重。代价：延迟从 <200ms 升到 1-2s，mega-stream 下可接受。
why_en: The first CDN snapshot is a ring buffer of the last 100-200 comments that overlaps what SSE just delivered, so the client dedupes by comment id with no gap, trading sub-200ms latency for 1-2s.
options_en: Clear the on-screen comments at switch time and rebuild the feed from the latest CDN snapshot from scratch.
The first CDN snapshot already holds the last 100-200 comments, overlapping the just-received SSE content, so the client dedupes by comment id.
Disconnect SSE, wait a few seconds before polling the CDN, giving the server time to prepare a snapshot.
Pop a prompt asking the user to manually refresh the page to load the CDN data.
q_en: What lets the client switch from SSE to CDN polling without missing or duplicating comments?
optionExplanations: 清屏重建会让观众眼前的评论流突然断裂重绘，正是「无缝切换」要避免的观感。
对，快照与 SSE 尾部重叠保证不漏，按评论 id 去重保证不重，切换对观众透明。
先断后等会造出一段真空期，观众看到评论流停住，违背无缝要求。
要用户手动刷新等于把无缝切换降级成一次可见的中断。
optionExplanations_en: Clearing and rebuilding tears the visible stream and redraws it, exactly the jank a seamless switch must avoid.
Right — the snapshot overlaps the SSE tail so nothing is lost, and comment-id dedup avoids repeats, keeping the switch invisible.
Disconnecting then waiting creates a dead gap where the stream visibly stalls, breaking the seamless requirement.
Asking the user to refresh downgrades a seamless switch into a visible interruption.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，基于标准 HTTP 的单向服务器推流协议
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE, Server-Sent Events, is a one-way server-to-client streaming protocol over plain HTTP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: ring buffer，固定容量的循环队列，只保留最近 N 条、旧的被新的覆盖
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ring buffer is a fixed-size circular queue that keeps only the most recent N items, overwriting the oldest.

scenario: 一个直播观看数刚越过 10 万阈值，系统自动从 SSE 实时推送翻转到 CDN 快照拉取。观众正盯着评论流，不能出现断流或空白重绘。
scenario_en: A live video just crossed the 100k-viewer threshold and the system auto-flips from SSE push to CDN snapshot polling while viewers watch the stream, so no gap or blank redraw is allowed.
